Hearing Laiku had come, Shen Weici paused slightly, then had a maid bring him in.

Laiku came in looking miserable, stood before Shen Weici, and slapped himself on the face: "Third Young Miss — this servant lost the letter."

Shen Weici looked at Laiku and told him not to be frightened — just tell her what had happened.

Hearing Shen Weici's gentle, steady voice, he calmed a little and said in a rush: "Just now this servant was hurrying toward the Earldom with the letter. Everything had been fine up until that point — no one on the road — but when I arrived at the Earldom and reached into my coat, the letter was gone."

"I turned myself inside out looking — nothing. I went back and walked the whole path again — still nothing. To this day I cannot work out where the letter could have disappeared."

Shen Weici heard this and frowned, going back over the contents of the letter in her mind. Fortunately, she had not mentioned her own identity in the letter, nor any reference to the Jian'an Marquis Manor. Even if someone with ill intentions had picked it up, they could not know who had written it.

Furthermore, she had written in the style of the practice volume, to let Zhang Yuanheng offer guidance — a style rarely used by women, making it difficult to guess whose hand it was.

Shen Weici felt somewhat relieved. She looked at Laiku standing there in a panic and said calmly: "I won't hold this against you. But next time be sure to keep it safely on your person — there can be no more mistakes like this."

Laiku nodded rapidly: "Third Young Miss may rest easy — it will never happen again."

He then looked at her carefully: "Could Third Young Miss not mention this to the Second Lord?"

Shen Weici smiled: "Don't worry."

Laiku let out a long breath of relief, beaming, and was about to leave.

Shen Weici stopped him: "If the courtyard runs out of charcoal and there isn't enough — what can be done?"

Laiku paused and said: "Each courtyard's monthly charcoal from the common fund is distributed in set amounts. If you go over, you have to buy it yourself."

He looked at Shen Weici: "Is Third Young Miss short of charcoal?"

Shen Weici smiled without answering, and only asked: "What does charcoal cost outside?"

Laiku thought: "Standard black charcoal is about fifty wen per catty. But that gives off a lot of smoke and fumes."

"Better quality nanmu charcoal is one hundred fifty wen. That's what the Manor uses. And above that, silver-thread charcoal isn't something ordinary people can afford — nearly one tael per catty."

Yuedeng made an involuntary exclamation: "That expensive?"

Laiku laughed: "There are even finer ones above that — the fragrant charcoal for ladies' hand warmers, or the walnut charcoal and olive charcoal used for brewing tea. The varieties are endless."

Shen Weici let Laiku go after that. The thought she had been entertaining of sending him to buy charcoal outside died quietly.

Yuedeng looked at Shen Weici: "Was Miss thinking of buying charcoal?"

Shen Weici said: "This month's courtyard ration has already been used. To go back and ask for more would be improper."

"But to go to Father again — the Second Lady would find out and cause trouble for me. And I've already gone once. Asking again so soon is not right."

"And if we buy charcoal with what's left of our monthly stipend, it won't buy much."

Yuedeng felt the difficulty: "Then how does Miss get through this month?"

"And as for Second Master — if things are hard for Miss, this servant won't let Miss take the fall for me."

Shen Weici pressed a hand to her brow with a sigh: "You spoke up on my behalf — and everything you said was completely right. It is Song Zhang who is being unreasonable."

"You did it for me. I will also look out for you. I won't let him do anything to you. Let's wait a few days and see."

Yuedeng looked at her mistress rubbing her temples with tired fingers, then at the flickering shadows beneath her lowered lashes — vivid pink, the silk-blue robe against skin white as snow, as lovely as a beauty before blossoming flowers.

She stared a moment, and felt, without cause, a kind of grief.

Like the grief of seeing a bright pearl coated in dust.

Her young mistress had never competed with anyone, was always quiet and composed, knew every propriety, and never sought to stand out. So why did one person after another come to torment her?

After more than a month in the Manor, she understood. Great families were all about status and birth. A whole den of wolves and tigers.

Shen Weici looked at the half-repaired garment on the low table — needles and thread scattered, the blue-green fabric catching the light in different hues. That vivid color seemed to mock her.

She could sew no more. Shen Weici rose and went to wash up, then settled into bed early.

In the Manor, even paper was something she had to use sparingly, to say nothing of books for leisure.

Shen Weici thought of the letter that had not been sent, and of Zhang Yuanheng's eager letters and his certain expectation of a reply. She did not want Zhang Yuanheng's enthusiasm to cool. Already out of her outer garments and in bed, she put them back on and got up, intending to write a second letter so Laiku could take it in the morning.

Yuedeng came in carrying the warming brick and immediately tried to stop her: "It's so cold — what is Miss getting up for? The charcoal from before is nearly spent too. Your chill had just barely cleared — if you catch another one, there's no silver left for medicine."

Shen Weici stopped. She naturally had no desire to fall ill again, and obediently lay back down.

She leaned against the soft pillow at her back and watched Yuedeng put the warming brick into her covers, while Yuedeng chattered on: "This Manor looks as though you'd never need to spend money on anything — but the moment you want to get anything done, everything costs silver."

"Even telling a servant to do a simple errand — you have to give a tip or they won't move. I don't know where that rule came from."

Shen Weici listened to her chatter. The warming brick had warmed her through, and she curled deeper under the covers.

Yuedeng then brought medicine to apply to the scratch on her jaw and gave a soft exclamation — she leaned in close to look, and said quietly: "Miss — this wound looks like it's almost healed already. It's scabbing over."

Yuedeng gently lifted the scab with her fingernail; it came away in a fleck of dark red, leaving a faint pink line.

Yuedeng quickly reapplied a layer of medicine: "The medicine the Second Lord gave really does work. Though looking at it, there isn't much left. I'm not sure how many more applications it can manage."

She said it, then immediately took it back: "No, no — best if we never need it again."

She looked at Shen Weici: "Does Miss want another warming brick?"

Shen Weici shook her head, and told Yuedeng to go to sleep as well.

chapters.title: The Banquet at the Zhang Household
chapters.content:
On the day of the banquet, Lady Wen specially sent someone to tell Shen Weici to dress with care — and even dispatched a matron to come and style her hair.

On ordinary days, Shen Weici wore simple hairstyles. Yuedeng did not know the capital's fashionable women's styles, and before Shen Weici came of age her hair had been worn half-up; now that she was of age and the hair should be pinned properly, the more elaborate styles were beyond Yuedeng, and Shen Weici had never minded, so nothing had been changed.

The matron Lady Wen had sent was swift and skilled. Standing behind Shen Weici and holding the flowing cascade of black hair, she said admiringly: "Third Young Miss has such soft, dark hair — smooth as silk. Once it's properly pinned, it will look beautiful."

Shen Weici herself had little investment in her hair, but she suddenly remembered the last time Lady Wen had sent the seamstress to make her clothing. She quietly called Yuedeng to stand nearby and watch — in case the matron tried something similar with her hair.

Yuedeng caught Shen Weici's meaning, stood to the side claiming she wanted to learn, and watched without blinking.

Fortunately the matron seemed genuinely focused on her work. With practiced hands, in no time at all she had styled Shen Weici's hair into a rather elaborate crossed-knot coif.

She then asked Shen Weici to bring out her ornaments. Shen Weici had Yuedeng fetch the box Shen Zhaozhao had sent. The matron looked at it and saw they were all somewhat outdated in the capital's fashion, but there was enough to work with.

She selected two jade hairpins and fastened them in, then bent to clip the jadeite earrings at Shen Weici's ears. She looked at the figure in the mirror — eyes dark as lacquer, lips red as cinnabar, a delicate oval face both fragile and lovely, with those peach-blossom eyes and the beauty-mark mole, like a spray of flowers heavy with dew.

In the way she held herself there was the poise of swaying autumn air, and in looks and bearing she was, if anything, a shade above Second Young Miss.

She kept this impression to herself, however, and straightened up, asking: "Does Third Young Miss have any pearl powder?"

Shen Weici shook her head: "I've never used it."

Matron Tan looked at her face — as white and smooth as fine mutton-fat jade. It made no difference either way.

She added: "The carriages are ready at the front gate. We leave at the hour of si. It must be nearly time — Third Young Miss should finish getting ready and make her way to the front gate."

With that, she had nothing more to say and left.

The moment the matron was gone, Yuedeng leaned close and gazed at Shen Weici with admiration: "Miss looks so beautiful dressed up."

But Shen Weici looked at Yuedeng with a faint furrow of concern: "By rights, at this kind of occasion, whether or not the Second Lady brings me along shouldn't matter much — given how little she cares for me, she really should not have bothered."

"And yet she sent a matron all the way to style my hair. That wasn't truly necessary. My ordinary appearance would have drawn no one's attention at a gathering like this."

"Besides, she clearly doesn't want me outshining Shen Zhaozhao. Usually she's glad for me to keep to myself — and yet this time she seems to be putting me on display."

Yuedeng went to fetch the white-ground cloud-and-water printed cloak and stood before Shen Weici to help her put it on: "Last time didn't the Second Lady say she wanted Miss to look respectable? I imagine it's for the sake of the Manor's reputation."

Shen Weici lowered her eyes as Yuedeng tied the cord at her throat. A breath of wind came in from outside, and she sighed: "I'm not so sure."

But she said no more about it. Once Shen Weici was ready, she set out with Yuedeng.

On this rare occasion of making a real effort with her appearance, the result was striking — a blue-ground pink-flower cloud-brocade skirt, with pink winding-branch patterns, her figure graceful and elegant. The smoke-blue earrings swayed against her face, and her skin in the daylight was startlingly white.

The maids of Linchun Courtyard all stared, and each one eagerly wanted to come along and see the world. But Shen Weici feared that too many maids might cause accidents; and besides, her maids had mostly been rough-work girls before, unfamiliar with outside propriety. If they blundered into some restriction or taboo, she would be hard pressed to manage the consequences.

So she said, gently but firmly, that they could come another time.

The maids were compliant and did not press.

At the front gate, a servant greeted Shen Weici with a smile: "Third Young Miss, this way please."

She followed and saw three carriages waiting at the gate, grandly appointed. The manservant up front reported: "Third Lady and First Master and Fourth Master are already in their carriage — Second Lady and Third Young Miss have not come yet."

Shen Weici asked casually: "What about Fourth Young Miss and Fifth Young Miss?"

The manservant paused at one of the carriages and held back the curtain, smiling: "Fourth Young Miss and Fifth Young Miss are not going."

Shen Weici heard this, gave a small nod, and bent to climb in.

When Yuedeng tried to follow, the manservant directed her to the rear carriage.

Inside the carriage it was quite spacious. Shen Weici sat and lifted a corner of the curtain to look outside. The carriage ahead was presumably the Second Branch's. The First Branch's Princess Consort Huimin was, as expected, absent again.

After a while, Lady Wen appeared with Shen Zhaozhao. Shen Weici let the curtain fall.

Lady Wen and Shen Zhaozhao boarded and the three of them sat together. Shen Weici spoke first, in a quiet voice: "Second Lady. Second Sister."

Lady Wen glanced at Shen Weici. The carriage light was dim; she looked cursorily — and then lifted the curtain to get a better look. Shen Weici sat with perfect composure by the window-side, hands resting on her knees with a handkerchief between her fingers, the lower halves of her fingers bare; her earrings brushed her white jade cheek, and as she gave a slight bow of the head and then raised her eyes again, it was a sight that startled Lady Wen.

She let the curtain fall. She gave a cool sound of acknowledgement and said no more.

Shen Weici also stayed quiet. She felt a gaze on her and knew it was Shen Zhaozhao from across the carriage, but did not raise her head.

Outside, the quiet gradually gave way to the lively sounds of street vendors calling their wares. Shen Weici had not been out of the Manor since arriving in the capital more than a month ago, and she was suddenly curious. Her fingers had just started to move toward the curtain when Lady Wen's cool, low voice came from across the carriage: "What — do you think so highly of yourself that you want the people outside to see you too?"

Shen Weici's hand stilled at these words. She withdrew her fingers.

At the Zhang household gate, firecrackers could already be heard from a distance; drawing closer, the sounds intensified, and there was a constant noise of voices. They had not yet descended from the carriage and already one could tell the occasion was lively beyond compare.

Maids came down from the rear carriages; a matron lifted the curtain to help those in the main carriage descend.

Shen Weici was last out. Stepping down, she could see numerous carriages drawn up before the Zhang household's great gate, with dedicated manservants guiding each one to its place.

Lady Wen ran into an acquaintance at the entrance and pulled the Third Lady-in-law Wang aside to chat. Shen Weici quietly followed at the rear.

She knew no one here and was afraid of causing some mistake.

A greeter came forward to lead Lady Wen and her party inside, but at that moment two eunuchs came running forward, shouting: "The Noble Consort arrives — make way!"

Everyone at the entrance froze and looked to one side. Two rows of armored guards escorted two exceptionally magnificent carriages forward, and people on either side stepped back of their own accord.

Shen Weici also looked over, and saw the procession was vast: ten eunuchs walking in front, some ten palace maids flanking the sides, and at the very head, mounted on horseback, was the Imperial Feathered Guard Commander Song Zhang.

Song Zhang wore a great red robe embroidered with coiling serpents, one hand holding the reins, the other a riding crop; two black-and-gold swords hung at his waist. His expression was haughty and languid, contemptuous of all below him.

Zhang Tingyi came hurrying forward from the crowd of guests, and following the eunuchs' announcement, knelt with everyone else: "We welcome the Noble Consort—"

chapters.title: Seeing Zhang Tingyi at the Banquet
chapters.content:
The gates of the Zhang household were thronged like a marketplace. Every person of rank and influence in the capital had come to pay court.

All the more so when Noble Consort Zhang arrived in person today — demonstrating the depth of the Emperor's favor. Those seeking to curry favor would be even more numerous.

A woman of the inner palace was normally not permitted to leave even when a family member died. Yet Noble Consort Zhang's mother was turning seventy, and the Emperor had granted her leave to attend the celebration — and moreover dispatched the Commander of the Imperial Feathered Guard himself to ride ahead and clear the path. This alone said everything about how favored Noble Consort Zhang was within the palace.

The Imperial Feathered Guard was charged with protecting the imperial family's movements, but having the Guard Commander personally escort someone was reserved only for the Emperor himself. Today's display had made it plain: the Emperor was giving the Zhang household every honor, and Zhang Tingyi's position at court was at its zenith.

The imperial carriage halted before the Zhang household gate. Song Zhang reined in his horse and looked around the assembly. His gaze passed over Shen Weici, who had knelt with the crowd — just a glance — and then he dismounted and went to Noble Consort Zhang's carriage, lifting the curtain for her.

The eunuch in front cried: "The Noble Consort descends — do not look directly upon her."

Everyone bowed their heads lower.

Noble Consort Zhang placed her hand in Song Zhang's and stepped down. She walked to the front, where her elder brother Zhang Tingyi stood: "Brother — take me to see Mother."

Zhang Tingyi hurried to fall in beside his sister and escort her inside.

Fifth Princess Zhao Rou, who had been following behind Noble Consort Zhang, looked back when she saw Song Zhang not following the group but walking the other way. She reached back and tugged his sleeve: "Why aren't you coming inside?"

Song Zhang glanced at the Fifth Princess and said with restrained patience, clasping his hands: "Your subject still needs to arrange the guards for Noble Consort's safety. I shall withdraw for now."

He did not wait for Zhao Rou to speak again, turned, and walked back toward the attendant guards.

Zhao Rou pouted at Song Zhang's retreating figure, stamped her foot in annoyance, then heard her mother calling for her ahead and quickly followed.

Once the Noble Consort had entered, the rest of the assembly finally rose from the ground.

Shen Weici stood among the crowd. She looked to one side — and saw Song Zhang standing before some twenty or so palace guards, his brows arched in arrogance, his red robe snapping in the wind as he issued what appeared to be instructions.

She looked away and then saw Lady Wen and Third Lady-in-law Wang heading into the residence. She hurried to catch up.

Behind her, Song Zhang seemed to sense something. He turned his head slightly — and caught just a glimpse of a trailing edge of smoky pink as it disappeared through the gate.

Shen Weici's party, once inside, was led by servants toward the rear garden. Only then did she understand that the Zhang household's grounds were a world unto themselves — fine trees clustered thickly, rare flowers blazed with color. On both sides rose soaring buildings cutting into the sky, with intricately carved ridgelines and embroidered balustrades, and everywhere stone steps wound up through clouds with white stone balustrades — all speaking of extraordinary wealth. Compared to the Jian'an Marquis Manor, this looked even grander.

The wives and female guests were led to the rear garden. Old Madam Zhang was seated in the main rear hall. Lady Wen, with no title or honorific to her name, was not eligible to sit in the same room as the Noble Consort. She could only go before Old Madam Zhang, say a few words of felicitation, show herself, and then withdraw.

Shen Weici followed behind Lady Wen and went inside. Looking up, she saw Noble Consort Zhang seated beside Old Madam Zhang at the head — and to either side were first-rank Duchesses, County Mistresses, imperially enfeoffed ladies, and the like.

Even though they were of the Jian'an Marquis household, in this hall they still had to kneel in ceremonial greeting before the Noble Consort. Only when the eunuch beside her announced they could rise were they permitted to stand and approach Old Madam Zhang to offer birthday congratulations.

After the full ceremony, Lady Wen nudged Shen Weici forward with a smile, asking her to wish the Old Madam long life before everyone.

Shen Weici noticed that even Shen Zhaozhao had not come forward and was still standing behind her mother, yet Lady Wen was pushing her to the front. She had little choice but to step up and offer a few phrases of good fortune and long life in a clear, warm voice.

She thought it would end there, and was about to step back — when Noble Consort Zhang spoke from the side: "Such a graceful and lovely young lady — and her voice is pleasant to listen to as well."

She smiled toward Lady Wen: "Second Lady Shen, you are fortunate."

Noble Consort Zhang was not unfamiliar with the Jian'an Marquis household. Before she had left home, the great families' daughters had all known one another, and besides, Princess Consort Huimin had married into the household, and Song Zhang was trusted by the Emperor. Her own daughter, the Fifth Princess, was the Emperor's choice for Song Zhang's betrothal. So she knew the household better than most.

Lady Wen, delighted by the Noble Consort's praise of Shen Weici, quickly agreed: "This is the Manor's Third Young Miss — only recently brought back to us. I am her stepmother and am raising her as my own. She is indeed a pleasing child."

Noble Consort Zhang, hearing Lady Wen's words, studied Shen Weici once more with narrow, appraising eyes. She had recently been thinking of selecting a gentle and composed side consort for the Fourth Prince, and the young woman before her was attractive enough in both face and bearing, and she was of the Jian'an Marquis household. If she had been the legitimate daughter it would have been better still — but she was concubine-born, which was a pity.

She withdrew her gaze and exchanged a few more courteous words with Lady Wen, then Lady Wen took Shen Weici and Shen Zhaozhao and withdrew.

Outside, matrons led them toward seating in the rear garden.

The rear garden was already full of guests. Across pavilions and terraces, richly dressed ladies and young misses stood in clusters of two, three, and four, talking and laughing. The air was thick with the scent of face powder.

Only now did Shen Weici truly understand that the capital was indeed full of high-ranking families at every turn. Lady Wen, who had been born into an aristocratic family, could only be counted as ordinary here.

Lady Wen went off to find an old friend, reminded Shen Zhaozhao not to wander too far so she could be found when the banquet started, and finally said to Shen Weici: "You're not familiar with anyone — just stay with Zhaozhao."

Shen Weici watched Lady Wen's retreating figure toward the pavilion, then saw Shen Zhaozhao waving to an acquaintance she recognized, clearly with no intention of looking after her. She took the hint and did not follow, but went to sit in a nearby pavilion.

The position was visible, not far from Lady Wen's pavilion, so Shen Weici could follow along easily if something came up.

And the pavilion had only two other young ladies already chatting inside, which was quiet enough.

She sat to one side, leaning against the railing, letting the cool breeze wash over her, looking out at the lake — its green surface rippling in soft waves.

Yuedeng whispered in awe beside her: "The Zhang household is really something. Look at this lake — you could actually go boating on it."

Just as she spoke, an excited voice nearby exclaimed: "Is that the Fourth Prince and General Song on the far bank?"

Shen Weici startled, and felt several women near her move to look across the water. She glanced in the same direction.

The two banks of the lake were not far apart. The women were all on this side; the men were across the water.

Shen Weici raised her eyes slightly and saw two figures standing at a balcony railing on the far bank — one in red, one in dark. Both were looking toward the lake, apparently in conversation.

Shen Weici could not make out their faces from across the water, but she guessed immediately that the figure in red was Song Zhang.

Then someone nearby murmured: "I hear General Song has no wife yet — because of an injury he suffered in the army. Lots of people have been saying so."

Another voice quickly cut in: "Be careful what you say. I've heard His Majesty intends to betroth the Fifth Princess to General Song. If that's true, would His Majesty arrange such a marriage?"

Shen Weici had heard enough by this point and let her gaze drift away from the far bank.

chapters.title: Encountering Song Zhang at the Zhang Estate
chapters.content:
After sitting for a while longer, Shen Weici noticed a maidservant standing beside the garden pavilion. She sent Yuedeng over to ask how much longer before the banquet would begin. Yuedeng returned to report that it would be nearly another hour before it started.

Shen Weici was unfamiliar with the estate and could not wander too far, so she remained in her spot, surrounded by faces she did not recognize.

As she let her gaze drift idly across the lake once more, she caught sight of a familiar figure on the opposite bank. The man stood among a small group, yet she had the distinct feeling that his eyes kept drifting back to her.

Because they were standing on a waterside pavilion that jutted out over the lake, they were not too far apart, and Shen Weici could clearly make out that the person across the water was Zhang Yuanheng.

She paused for a moment, then saw that Zhang Yuanheng was also looking at her — smiling at her from within the crowd, his bright eyes shining. In the midst of this unfamiliar, unsettling environment, that smile brought her a measure of calm. Thinking that she now had someone steady and dependable by her side, she could not help but let a smile touch her own eyes in return.

Zhang Yuanheng was momentarily stunned by that smile. He noticed, too, that Shen Weici was dressed more elaborately today than her usual understated style, which made her look even more striking. The jade hairpin nestled in her dark hair and the earrings swaying beside her face were simply breathtaking.

Someone called his name twice and received no response. That person followed Zhang Yuanheng's gaze and asked with a laugh: "Who is Brother Zhang looking at? You've gone completely dazed."

"Is that some beauty over there? Should I call out to her, so she knows of Brother Zhang's feelings?"

Only then did Zhang Yuanheng come back to his senses, and he turned to his companions with a sheepish bow. "Gentlemen, please don't tease me."

But then he saw his friend craning his neck to peer across the water and quickly moved to block his line of sight. "What's so worth looking at? Surely talking with me is more important than ogling beauties?"

For his trouble, he got a punch in the chest. "You were the one not paying attention."

Shen Weici watched Zhang Yuanheng and his companions banter with a suppressed smile. When she turned her head, however, her eyes swept over something and her expression stiffened.

On the covered walkway across the way, Song Zhang stood talking with a group of people. For no clear reason she could name, she had the distinct sense that he was watching her with those cold, icy eyes of his.

She had done nothing, and yet she felt as though she had been caught doing something shameful.

After sitting for a while longer, the covered walkway across the way was empty of people. When she turned again, she saw the women nearby rise and look toward the front. Following their gaze, she spotted the Imperial Consort leading the Fifth Princess, along with several noblewomen who were close to her, heading off to stroll through the Chaolu Garden.

A great procession of eunuchs and maidservants swept around them like a dark, pressing crowd. Wherever they passed, everyone stepped aside.

Then she noticed a dainty, richly dressed young woman reaching out repeatedly to tug at Song Zhang's sleeve as he walked alongside the procession. The girl tilted her head up as if speaking to him and even reached out her fingers to touch the sword at his waist.

That must be the Fifth Princess the others had just been whispering about.

Song Zhang's expression was unreadable — probably still that unpredictable shift between displeasure and indifference — yet he appeared to be tolerating the Fifth Princess's indiscriminate pawing at him.

Someone nearby murmured quietly: "They say the Fifth Princess is willful and spoiled, but looking at her beside General Song, she doesn't seem quite like the rumors say."

Another replied in an undertone: "Rumors don't rise from nothing. Perhaps she's only like this in front of General Song."

Shen Weici watched in silence as the procession moved past. When she turned again, she happened to catch a glimpse of Madam Wen heading toward the rear main courtyard with a maidservant, while Shen Zhaohao was nowhere to be seen nearby. After a short while, she saw Wencui — Madam Wen's head maidservant — standing in the open, scanning the area as if searching for someone. At last Wencui's eyes met Shen Weici's, and she came hurrying over.

Shen Weici looked on and stood up, bringing Yuedeng along. She watched Wencui stride toward her and say: "Third Miss, please don't wander off. Come with me — the Madam may be asking for you shortly."

With that, Wencui led Shen Weici toward the hall where they had paid their respects to Old Madam Zhang.

The courtyard ahead was wide and open. Shen Weici asked: "Is Second Elder Sister not coming?"

Wencui glanced at Shen Weici and smiled slightly. "The Second Miss is probably deep in lively conversation with the other young ladies right now. The Madam said to let the Second Miss be."

As they were speaking, a maidservant named Xiaohong came out from inside and greeted Shen Weici with a smile: "Third Miss, the Madam is asking you to come in and sit with her."

At these words, Shen Weici felt something was not quite right.

How was it that Madam Wen was keeping her by her side? Wouldn't Shen Zhaohao be a more fitting choice?

Shen Weici was about to ask, but Xiaohong urged her with a smile: "The Madam is still waiting, Third Miss — please hurry."

Shen Weici had no choice but to follow Xiaohong inside.

The place, which had been lively just a short while ago, was now somewhat quieter.

While sitting in the pavilion earlier, she had overheard a fair bit of gossip — that Zhang Tingyi had married twice and kept countless women beside him, yet had only one son, and that son was simple-minded. Someone had even whispered that the foolish boy might not be his.

Now that the Imperial Consort Zhang had left, the only people remaining by Old Madam Zhang's side were longtime friends of hers, a few fawning noblewomen, and some distant relatives.

Shen Weici looked at Madam Wen's brilliantly smiling face. She had never seen the woman smile so ingratiatingly before. This, she concluded, must be a case of flattery in action.

Bearing the weight of glances from all sides, she walked quietly over to Madam Wen's side. When Madam Wen saw her, she smiled and said: "Come sit beside me. You're not familiar with anyone here, so it's better you stay close."

Shen Weici looked at Madam Wen's warm, smiling face, pressed her lips together, and sat down beside her.

A woman nearby smiled at Madam Wen: "How kind-hearted you are — even this generous toward a concubine-born daughter."

Madam Wen replied: "Her mother is gone, so I raise her as my own. What does birth status matter?"

The noblewomen present all burst into praise for Madam Wen's magnanimity.

Shen Weici listened in silence, her face betraying no expression whatsoever.

After a while, someone entered from outside.

The newcomer was dressed in a purple everyday robe, appeared to be around fifty years of age, and carried himself with an alert, upright, capable bearing. His ornamentation was lavish — a golden crown, a jade-studded belt, and three or four jade thumb rings on his fingers. Several attendants followed behind him.

He walked directly to Old Madam Zhang, who sat at the head of the room, and paid his respects, then went forward to ask whether anything had been overlooked in the arrangements.

Old Madam Zhang smiled: "Don't trouble yourself with this — go back out and tend to the guests. Just rein in that temper of yours and drink a little less."

Zhang Tingyi smiled, then lingered a moment longer beside his mother before preparing to leave. Suddenly, Madam Wen stood up and pulled Shen Weici forward with her: "Weici, come quickly and pay your respects to Master Zhang."

Shen Weici was tugged to her feet by Madam Wen. Her gaze fell on the cluster of embroidered flowers at the center of Zhang Tingyi's chest, and she had no choice but to steel herself and speak: "Greetings, Master Zhang."

Zhang Tingyi heard a soft, melodious voice and startled, looking down to find the source. He saw gently downcast brows and eyes, and earrings that shimmered against a fair complexion — the slant of those eye corners carried the grace of a lotus. She was radiant beyond description.

Zhang Tingyi stared, momentarily entranced. He had always been a man who coveted beauty, and his mind stirred at once. He turned to Madam Wen and asked: "Is this a young lady from the Marquis's household?"

Madam Wen, noting the expression on Zhang Tingyi's face, smiled: "She was just brought back from the countryside to the Marquis's estate. Her mother has passed away. She has just reached the age of adulthood and is waiting to be matched."

Zhang Tingyi, hearing those words, understood their meaning well enough. He could see Madam Wen had deliberately brought this girl to stand before him, and when she mentioned "waiting to be matched," what else remained unclear?

His own position was at its zenith these days, and those seeking to flatter him were beyond counting — there was never any shortage of people sending beauties his way.

But some were too low in birth to be anything but a concubine, while others of better standing were lacking in looks. This beauty before him had the Marquis's estate behind her, and though she was concubine-born, her appearance was such, and her background clean enough, that there was truly nothing to object to.

His eyes traveled slowly over Shen Weici, and when they landed on her slender waist, a heat kindled behind them. He looked up at Madam Wen with a smile: "I was just exchanging a few words with Shen Zhongzheng out in the front courtyard. I'll call on your estate another day. I should get back to the guests for now — please make yourself at home, Madam Shen."

With that, Zhang Tingyi turned and walked out, but not before letting his gaze linger on Shen Weici one last time.

Once Zhang Tingyi had gone, Madam Wen pulled Shen Weici down to sit beside her.

Shen Weici tilted her head slightly and studied Madam Wen's face — that face which was ordinarily neither warm nor cold toward her, now all smiles and easy satisfaction. She turned her gaze away.

chapters.title: Leaving Early
chapters.content:
After the banquet, groups of two and three women stood chatting, and it seemed as though things would not wind down for some time yet.

Yuedeng sidled up to Shen Weici's ear and whispered: "Earlier, while I was sitting in the carriage, I spotted a pawnshop down a street behind several alleys outside the Zhang estate's gate. Should I slip away now to pawn the item?"

"I still have the fox fur tucked against me."

Shen Weici glanced over at Madam Wen, who was still deep in conversation with the other women, and said quietly: "It isn't safe for you to go alone. Stay close to me for now — I'll see if we can leave early."

She noticed that Shen Zhaohao was not keeping Madam Wen company at the moment either, so she touched her forehead and went to Madam Wen's side: "Mother, it's quite windy outside. I've developed a headache. May I head home first?"

Madam Wen noticed that Shen Weici had addressed her as "Mother" in front of all these people, preserving both their dignities — that showed good sense. Besides, she had already seen the way Zhang Tingyi had looked at Shen Weici. The deed was done. So she smiled in reply: "I still have a while here. If your head hurts, I'll have a matron escort you back."

Madam Wen's face was all smiles, and she seemed perfectly accommodating. Shen Weici looked at that smile, pressed her own lips into a faint curve, and nodded obediently: "Then I'll take my leave."

Madam Wen gave a sound of assent and sent Changnanny along to see Shen Weici out.

The men and the female guests had been seated separately at the banquet, and the exit for the women went through another small path behind the inner courtyard, leading out through a side gate.

When they arrived, Changnanny went to speak with the attendants at the door, who busily and politely went off to summon the Shen estate's carriage.

Once the carriage arrived, Changnanny smiled at Shen Weici: "Please board, Third Miss."

Shen Weici made a sound of agreement, then glanced sideways at Changnanny and asked: "Will Changnanny be returning with us?"

Changnanny smiled: "I still need to attend to the Madam. Don't worry, Third Miss — the coachman is an old hand from the Marquis's estate, and there are guards following behind. Nothing will happen."

Shen Weici turned her gaze to the guard who had taken up position at the rear, a powerfully built man who looked every part the fighter. She smiled and boarded the carriage with Yuedeng.

Once inside, Yuedeng could no longer hold back the questions she had been bottling up: "Miss, don't you think the Second Madam was unusually agreeable today?"

"Could it be that after what happened last time with the Second Master, the Second Madam feels she's been harsh and is starting to treat Miss better?"

The smile had already faded from Shen Weici's face. The suspicions circling in her mind continued to turn, though she said nothing of them to Yuedeng, only saying quietly: "Remember this: someone who doesn't like you won't suddenly start liking you overnight. Caution and care are always the wiser path."

As she spoke, Shen Weici's dark brows furrowed slightly. Her clear, still eyes drifted unfocused, and her fingers tightened around the handkerchief in her hand as her thoughts grew heavy.

The sounds of people gradually rose outside. Yuedeng quickly lifted the curtain to look out and spotted a pawnshop, then hurriedly pulled aside the inner curtain at the front of the carriage and called to the coachman: "Hey, stop here for a moment."

Old Zhong quickly pulled on the reins and the carriage came to a halt. Yuedeng was just about to climb down when the guard walking behind came forward and spoke to Shen Weici through the carriage curtain: "Third Miss, if you need something, just tell me — it would be better not to stop in a crowd like this."

Shen Weici lifted one corner of the curtain and raised her eyes to the guard standing just outside, then spoke in a gentle, warm tone: "I came out without hand warmers and I'm craving candied chestnuts. I'd like to send my maidservant to buy some."

"She spotted them — they're just across the street. It won't take long."

It was the golden hour of the afternoon outside, and the guard found himself looking at a few slender, snow-white fingers and that luminous, fair face, so bright he could barely meet her gaze.

Then he took in her smiling eyes and those earrings dancing in the afternoon light, with even the tip of her nose glowing warmly — and his heart started hammering in his chest.

He had heard there was a Third Miss newly arrived at the Marquis's estate from the countryside, supposedly coarse and wild. Meeting her now in person, all he found was that gentle, soft voice — no hint of coarseness — let alone a face like hers.

He was momentarily struck dumb, his face warming from the contagion of her smile. He looked away and, going along with her words, said: "Candied chestnuts are just right for this time of year. I know of a shop whose chestnuts are quite popular with the ladies. The Second Miss often sends someone there. Would you like me to go fetch some for the Third Miss?"

Shen Weici smiled: "How could I put you to that trouble? Besides, I'm not particular — my maidservant knows my taste, so let her go buy some from across the street."

"It's just a quick errand."

The guard, without even stopping to think, nodded along with her words. "All right."

He even thoughtfully held back the curtain for Yuedeng.

Yuedeng climbed out of the carriage. Shen Weici glanced at her and reminded her: "Buy what you need and come straight back. No dawdling."

Yuedeng smiled sweetly: "Don't worry, Miss."

And with that, she spun around and headed across the street.

Shen Weici watched the guard turn his gaze toward the other side of the street. She loosened her grip on the handkerchief, then let out a soft sound of surprise. The guard turned back at once, and she looked at him with wide, startled eyes: "The wind has blown my handkerchief away."

The guard quickly looked down and spotted the white square of cloth some twenty or thirty feet ahead, blown there by the wind. He hurried over to retrieve it for her.

The truth was, Yuedeng going to pawn the white fox fur collar was not anything shameful in itself — but it had been a gift, after all. If word got out, people in the Marquis's estate would inevitably say that Linchun Courtyard had fallen on such hard times that they were pawning a fur collar. If those words were then used to lecture her, Madam Wen would hear of it and find cause to make trouble.

She could certainly tear off that mask of false virtue, but she was alone and without backing, and she was still wary of having her marriage prospects used as a leash around her neck. Keeping up a surface of harmony was still the wisest course — there was no point in open confrontation.

The handkerchief was placed back in her hand. Shen Weici smiled and thanked the guard, then asked: "I'm still new to the Marquis's estate and there's much I don't understand. May I ask — if I want to go out in the future, am I free to do so at will?"

The guard smiled: "Certainly not at will. The Third Miss belongs to the Second Branch, so you'd need permission from the Second Master and Second Madam, and you'd have to take your token to the front gate. You also must have a guard with you — you can't go out alone."

Shen Weici actually knew these rules well enough already; she was simply looking for something to say. She asked again: "Does the Marquis's estate and the Zhang estate frequently see each other?"

The guard looked at Shen Weici, slightly puzzled by the sudden question, and laughed: "That I wouldn't know."

Shen Weici nodded. The afternoon light fell across her eyes, making her squint slightly. She was just casting about for another topic when a dark shadow suddenly pressed close, and the carriage window rattled as someone's waist bumped against it — the faint clinking coming from a sword hilt. Looking at that level, she found herself staring directly at the person's waist.

A gold-fitted sword belt, with a dagger thrust through it. The red gemstone on the dagger blazed like fire, stinging Shen Weici's eyes. She raised her gaze.

The one standing before her carriage window was none other than Song Zhang.

Shen Weici instinctively clenched her fingers. She had thought he should still be at the Zhang estate — how had he ended up here?

chapters.title: Shameless
chapters.content:
Song Zhang had been accompanying the Fourth Prince back to the Prince's manor in Changxing Ward when his carriage passed by and he recognized in an instant the Marquis's estate carriage stopped at the roadside. He caught sight of the curtain lifted at the carriage window, a snow-white, shapely hand showing through the gap, and the embroidered silk handkerchief between those fingers seemed to be toying with the guard's heartstrings.

He watched her deliberately let the handkerchief fall so the guard would pick it up, then turn toward him with a smile of practiced sweetness. Song Zhang could not help but concede that Shen Weici possessed a formidable arsenal of tricks.

No doubt the delicate, helpless face she had shown him was equally calculated — weeping pitifully in front of others while enduring slights with mournful restraint, on purpose losing a couplet duel she had clearly been capable of winning, and giving off that air of coy resistance. The techniques for drawing a man in were first-rate.

Right there at the Zhang estate banquet she had not forgotten to cast glances across the water at Zhang Yuanheng, either.

Song Zhang's eyes turned cold and flat. His well-defined fingers gripped the rim of the carriage window as he bent slightly at the waist to look into the carriage at Shen Weici.

That face had already retreated further into the carriage. In the dim half-light inside, her brows arched like distant mountains and her lips seemed to hold a cherry within — her dark hair carried the grace of moonlight and wind. Even he was momentarily caught off guard.

Truly a face made to bewitch and ensnare.

The contempt and disdain in his eyes were completely undisguised: "Are you really so desperate for men? Do you even set your sights on a mere guard?"

Shen Weici heard these words with no beginning and no end, and her expression stiffened for a moment. She could not fathom how such unreasonable words had come out of his mouth.

She met Song Zhang's eyes and said quietly: "I don't understand what Young Lord Song means, and I ask that Young Lord Song mind his words."

Song Zhang was almost provoked into a laugh by Shen Weici's reply. He did actually sneer aloud: "Don't understand?"

"Was it not you who deliberately dropped your handkerchief to entice a man just now? And who was it smiling at a man across the water at the Zhang estate? Shen Weici, where is your sense of shame?"

"How can a woman be so wanton? Do you truly cannot live without a man?"

Shen Weici's face went pale at what she heard. She stared at Song Zhang in disbelief, her voice trembling slightly: "It is your own mind that is filthy, and so everything you see appears filthy."

"If I talk to someone, if I smile at someone, does that make it seduction?"

"Young Lord Song pays such close attention to me — more than I deserve. Since the Young Lord sees me as such a woman, then in future, Young Lord Song need not look at me at all. I, for my part, will only keep myself at a greater distance from Young Lord Song."

This time it was Song Zhang whose expression shifted. The darkness in those black eyes passed through several permutations before he ground out cold words: "Whatever you are, do you think you're worth my attention? I simply find your manner of seducing men distasteful."

"Throwing yourself at every man you lay eyes on."

Shen Weici had never been insulted in such a manner in her life. Her eyes reddened, and she blinked several times before speaking in a small voice: "Young Lord Song may think poorly of me as he likes — that's no concern of mine, and I never wished to have any entanglement with Young Lord Song."

"I also ask that Young Lord Song not trouble me in future, given that I am clearly so unworthy in his eyes."

"And I would ask Young Lord Song to please make clear: who exactly did I seduce? And who did I throw myself at?"

"You cannot simply slander me on empty words."

Song Zhang watched those eyes of Shen Weici's gradually turn red, saw the shimmer of moisture in those alluring eyes — he tightened his grip and answered through clenched teeth, his expression dark: "You know very well yourself."

"That I did not say it outright was already giving you face. Consider it a warning to behave yourself in future."

Shen Weici saw that Song Zhang's words were growing more and more unreasonable. She fought back the threat of tears: "I don't understand."

Song Zhang's cold gaze was now entirely filled with Shen Weici's soft features. Just moments ago, she had smiled at a guard with eyes soft as misty rain — and now that he had exposed her, she was still wearing that same fragile, yielding manner, as though she wanted to soften his heart.

He let out a cold laugh, just about to speak, when Fourth Prince Li Zhaoyi's voice sounded from behind: "Song Zhang, what are you doing over there? Why haven't you come back yet?"

Hearing the Fourth Prince's voice and the approaching footsteps behind him, Song Zhang's thoughts flickered to Shen Weici's nature. Knowing she would recognize Li Zhaoyi as the Fourth Prince, she would probably be delighted to sidle right up to him and bat her eyes.

The Prince's manor outranked even an Earl's estate.

This thought lasted only an instant. Then, before Shen Weici's watching eyes, he yanked the curtain shut with a swift pull, turned around, and ushered the Fourth Prince on toward Changxing Ward.

Shen Weici stared blankly at the curtain that had just fallen in front of her. In the dim interior of the carriage, she looked at it for a moment, then propped her head on her hand and closed her eyes in exhaustion.

Yuedeng came back before long with the candied chestnuts and gave a few to the guard with a smile.

Then she lifted the curtain and climbed back into the carriage, and at once she found Shen Weici with reddened eyes. She hurried to sit beside her: "Miss, what's the matter?"

Shen Weici pushed aside the thought of Song Zhang's words, let go of the hand she had been pressing to her forehead, dabbed her handkerchief against her eyes, then lowered it and shook her head. She turned to Yuedeng and asked quietly: "How much did you pawn it for?"

Yuedeng pulled a plump little pouch from inside her clothes and squinted at Shen Weici with a grin. "Would Miss like to weigh it in her hand?"

Shen Weici smiled: "Just tell me."

Yuedeng made an exaggerated show of holding up three fingers. "Thirty taels!"

"Miss! I had no idea that white fox fur was worth so much. They were truly generous at the Yongan Marquis's estate."

Shen Weici allowed herself a thin smile: "Perhaps to them, this much money isn't worth much at all."

Yuedeng wrinkled her nose: "That's true."

"I've also worked it out — even if we buy twenty jin of nanmu charcoal, that's only three taels. We can absolutely afford it now."

Yuedeng said this and then caught herself, staring at Shen Weici in exaggerated wonder: "Why does it feel like three taels suddenly isn't that much money anymore? Back in Yuyang, three taels could buy two months' worth of grain."

Shen Weici smiled faintly, then drifted off into her own thoughts.

Back at the Marquis's estate, Shen Weici went directly to sit at the desk and spread out a sheet of white paper.

Yuedeng watched her movements and couldn't help but ask: "Is Miss writing a letter again?"

Shen Weici silently dipped a brush in ink, her gaze unfocused, then looked out at the courtyard garden.

The tree longs for stillness, but the wind will not cease.

After a long time of deliberation, she finally set brush to paper.

This time she wrote slowly, weighing each word, so that the letter's contents would not seem too abrupt or presumptuous.

When she had finished, she watched the ink dry in silence, then carefully folded the letter and sealed it in an envelope.

She handed the letter to Yuedeng, with a reminder: "Make sure Laifu holds onto this the entire way this time — he must not lose it. Tell him to keep it in his hand the whole journey, not to slip up again."

Yuedeng nodded, then asked: "Should I have Laifu also pick up some charcoal from outside while he's at it?"

Shen Weici shook her head: "No rush — we can see about that tomorrow."

Yuedeng paused and nodded, tucking the letter into her bosom before going out to deliver it.

Outside, Hexia came in carrying hot tea: "It's cold out, Miss — don't sit by the window. Come sit inside."

Shen Weici took the teacup from Hexia's hands, smiled, rose, and went to sit on the couch inside.

She sipped slowly, then noticed the plum blossoms arranged in the porcelain vase on the stand across the room, drifting a quiet fragrance.

Shen Weici asked: "Are the plum blossoms blooming?"

Hexia smiled: "They're not at their most brilliant yet, but a few early ones are opening. While Miss was out today, we girls had nothing to do, so we went and cut a few branches to bring inside."

"We even collected some plum blossom dew. The tea Miss is drinking now was brewed with it."

Shen Weici was surprised. She lowered her gaze to look at the tea in her cup, and a delicate fragrance rose to meet her. She smiled: "No wonder it tastes so warm and faintly sweet — quite lovely."

Hexia replied: "If Miss likes it, tomorrow we'll go and collect some more. There's a whole stretch of plum trees in the back garden."

"They say drinking plum blossom dew tea regularly is good for one's health."

Shen Weici smiled: "There's no need to fuss over it so early in the morning. I'm not really that refined a person."

"But you all following me like this — I fear you've been put to hardship."

Hexia hurried to say: "All of us girls say it's wonderful serving Miss. It's nothing like before, when the old nannies were always scolding us. It's peaceful here, and Miss has such a good temper — we'd be more than glad to stay with Miss always."

Shen Weici pressed her lips together and let out a quiet, wistful sigh.

In Guansong Courtyard, Song Zhang sat under the lamp and looked at the letter envelope that Minghé had brought him, giving him a sidelong glance. "You're fast."

Minghé smiled and said: "I originally intended to bring back all the letters the Third Miss sent to Zhang Yuanheng, but unfortunately, I couldn't find where Zhang Yuanheng had hidden the others no matter how long I searched."

"This one today happened to still be sitting on his desk when he hadn't put it away yet — that's how I was able to get it."

Song Zhang listened to Minghé's words, his gaze falling on the letter. The longer he read, the darker his expression became, until at last a teacup shattered.

chapters.title: Feigning Illness
chapters.content:
The next morning, Shen Weici did not rise as early as she usually did. She lay in bed and called for Yuedeng, then propped herself up slightly and told her: "Go to the Second Madam's quarters and tell her I've taken ill — my body feels weak and I cannot get out of bed."

"Also say that I fell when I came home yesterday and scratched my face on a tree branch, so I cannot come to pay my respects today. I'll go over to apologize tomorrow."

Yuedeng was startled by Shen Weici's words and immediately looked at her face, searching it carefully. Seeing not the faintest trace of any injury, she asked: "Miss, your face isn't scratched at all. And are you truly ill?"

Shen Weici took Yuedeng's hand in her cool fingers: "Whether or not I'm genuinely ill doesn't really matter. Just go and tell the Second Madam exactly what I said."

"If she asks you anything, make the illness sound serious. Also mention the scratch on my face — describe it as a red mark — and be sure to bring up the matter of my knees hurting, but don't breathe a word about Shen Zhaohao coming to my courtyard and ruining the charcoal."

"If the Second Madam comes herself, you can speak of it then — not before."

Yuedeng looked at Shen Weici in confusion: "Why go about it like this?"

"What if the Second Madam comes and sees that Miss has no scratch on her face?"

Shen Weici's loose dark hair tumbled over her shoulders. Her calm, composed eyes were cool and clear in the candlelight: "Don't worry about that."

"There's a reason for all of this, and I'll explain it to you slowly later. For now, just go to the Second Courtyard and say what I told you. And make sure the other girls outside say the same — don't let anyone blurt out the wrong thing."

Yuedeng said yes and immediately called out toward the door for a lantern, then headed off to the Second Courtyard.

Once Yuedeng had gone, Shen Weici lay back down on the bed, on her side as before. She lay there in her white single-layered underrobe, one arm resting on top of the quilt, her eyes half-open, half-closed, thinking back over every event since the day she had first stepped through the Marquis's estate gates.

She was lost in thought when anxious voices sounded from behind the screen: "Miss is ill?"

Shen Weici turned her head and saw that it was Hexia and Hosexiang. The two girls had apparently heard a word from Yuedeng and, noticing that their Miss had not gone out, had come rushing in to check on her.

Shen Weici pressed her hand to her mouth and forced out several coughs that sounded labored, then spoke as though barely able to muster the energy: "It's nothing serious. Don't worry about me."

Hexia saw that Shen Weici seemed to struggle just to speak, and couldn't help but say: "How can we not worry? Miss looks like this — I wish I could take the illness onto myself instead."

"Once the sky brightens, I'll go and summon the estate physician to take a look, or else go to the Second Madam's quarters — someone must come and look after you."

Shen Weici closed her eyes without a word, as if she had drifted off to sleep.

Hexia and Hosexiang, seeing that she was clearly unwell, did not dare disturb her and retreated outside, standing anxiously at the courtyard gate to wait for Yuedeng's return with word on the Second Madam's reaction.

After a while, they saw in the distance a large group approaching — matrons on both sides carrying lanterns, lighting the path brightly ahead. It was none other than Madam Wen herself.

Hexia was delighted and hurried with Hosexiang to stand at the courtyard entrance to receive her.

This was the first time Madam Wen had ever come to Shen Weici's Linchun Courtyard. She cast a glance at the broken-down lantern hanging at the courtyard gate, then looked at the bleak and desolate yard, and her brows creased slightly.

The maidservants at the front entrance quickly lifted the curtain when they saw Madam Wen enter.

But when she stepped inside, not a whisper of warmth greeted her — just an all-pervading chill. Madam Wen, accustomed to living in warm, well-heated rooms, felt the cold seep in from all sides and wrap around her neck.

She did not go past the screen to the inner room. Instead, she turned to Yuedeng with a frown: "Did your Master not receive charcoal recently? Why has no fire been lit? Are you lazy girls being negligent toward your mistress?"

Yuedeng, hearing these words of blame, immediately dropped to her knees: "Second Madam does us a great injustice. It is not that Linchun Courtyard won't light charcoal fires — it is that there is no charcoal to light."

Madam Wen let out a cold huff and pointed at Yuedeng: "What do you mean by that? The charcoal the Master sent — where is it? Did you girls secretly take it for yourselves?"

Yuedeng had not expected that when she went to report her Miss's illness, Madam Wen would personally lead a retinue all the way here, let alone suddenly bring up the charcoal. And after she herself had been the one to intercept it — the irony was not lost on the girls standing below.

Keeping her Miss's words in mind, Yuedeng raised her head and began to cry in earnest: "How would we dare steal the charcoal? The Second Master did send charcoal, but when the Second Miss came by last time, she brought several matrons with her and they stomped all of Miss's charcoal to pieces and poured water on top — every bit of it was ruined."

She wiped her tears with her sleeve and wept on: "Miss has been keeping this to herself the whole time. She told us not to go around saying it, lest the other courtyards hear and misunderstand. So she has simply borne it in silence."

"And now that winter has truly arrived, with this bitter cold, Miss has had a weak constitution from childhood, prone to the cold. Yesterday at the Zhang estate, Miss was waiting in an open pavilion the whole time and came home with hands as stiff as boards. She doesn't even have a hand warmer, but she never complains — she just endures it. This very morning she still intended to get up and pay her respects to the Second Madam."

"But when we maidservants helped Miss get up and she wasn't even fully dressed yet, she fainted on the spot. That's when I ran to your quarters to report."

Hexia and Hosexiang, listening to Yuedeng's account, silently admired her. They dabbed at their own eyes in turn.

Madam Wen watched this scene with a sour expression, then heard Yuedeng's words and felt her own face shift slightly. The question she had asked had now turned around and left her nowhere to retreat.

She kept her expression cool and maintained her composure. She turned to Changnanny beside her: "Since there is no charcoal in the room, have thirty jin sent over from my stores. Falling ill from the cold would not do."

Changnanny acknowledged this, stepped back two paces, and quietly gave the order to a maidservant.

Madam Wen then gathered her sleeves and passed through the screen decorated with magnolias carved in stone to enter the inner room. Through the gauze half-curtain of the pale yellow bed canopy, with its trailing tassels, she could just make out the figure sleeping inside.

Madam Wen asked: "Is she awake?"

Yuedeng got up from the floor and went to lift the bed curtain, peering inside. She heard a few coughs and saw the slow flutter of eyelids. Understanding at once, she called out softly: "Miss, the Second Madam has come to see you."

She gave Shen Weici's arm a gentle nudge.

Shen Weici coughed more heavily, as though roused by Yuedeng's push. She propped herself up from the bed, then turned her head to look out. When she saw Madam Wen, her eyes grew red and her voice came out hoarse: "It's so cold outside — you needn't have come all this way for me, Second Madam."

"I should be the one going to pay my respects to Second Madam."

Madam Wen studied the girl — her wan, sickly face, white robes, and dark ink hair in the wavering lamplight, almost luminous as the moon — and heard the humble, yielding words she spoke. A complicated feeling stirred somewhere inside her.

She did not like Shen Weici, it was true. But from the time the girl had entered the estate until now, she had always been quiet and unobtrusive, never causing any trouble. And it was always Zhaohao who bullied her.

Still, this girl's nature was also convenient: at least she was easy to control.

The reason Madam Wen had come today, if truth be told, was that she feared Shen Weici might be gravely ill. More importantly, she was afraid the scratch on her face might mar her appearance and ruin things with Zhang Tingyi, who would be coming to see her in a few days. Otherwise, she would not have bothered making this trip.

Madam Wen arranged her face into an expression of concern, walked to the bedside, and looked closely at Shen Weici's face. When she saw not even a trace of a scar, she frowned and asked: "Did your maidservant not say your face was scratched?"

Shen Weici gave a small cough before replying: "Yesterday my face was scraped by a tree branch and left a red mark. My maidservant was worried for me and put some medicine on it, and it seems to have healed this morning. It was a small thing — I didn't expect her to tell the Second Madam about it and cause you worry."

Madam Wen saw that Shen Weici's face was uninjured and let out a breath of relief. Zhang Tingyi had fallen for this face — she could not afford anything to go wrong with it.

She looked at Shen Weici again and sighed: "Why didn't you come and tell me what Zhaohao's people did to your charcoal?"

"The winters in the capital are dreadfully cold. With no charcoal in your rooms, how could you not fall ill?"

chapters.title: Alone With Zhang Yuanheng
chapters.content:
Hearing Madam Wen's words, Shen Weici gave two more small, carefully timed coughs, then said softly: "I know Second Elder Sister didn't mean anything by it, and I know it's only because of Second Madam's kind heart that I was allowed to stay here. I would not dare bring more trouble to Second Madam."

"That Second Madam has come to see me today is already more than I deserve."

Madam Wen studied Shen Weici's face — downcast eyes, soft and yielding — and couldn't tell whether the girl's words were sincere or whether some resentment lay hidden beneath. She observed her for a long moment before finally saying: "You needn't be like this. We are family — there's no such thing as troubling or not troubling."

"From now on, if anything is the matter, come and find me directly. If anything in the courtyard is lacking, come and ask me for it. Surely I would not neglect you."

Shen Weici was so moved by these words that she shed tears. Her already-reddened eyes brimmed with two crystal drops, and she looked at Madam Wen: "Weici is someone with no one to rely on. It is only through Second Madam's charity that I was taken in. Now, for the first time, I feel as though I have come ashore after drifting on water — I have a place to anchor my heart."

Madam Wen was momentarily taken aback. She had only said a few pleasantries meant for appearances' sake — she had not expected Shen Weici to be so moved.

Her mind grew more at ease.

She smiled: "Rest well these next two days. Don't worry about morning greetings until you're better. I'll also have the estate physician come take a look, and have a few medicinal prescriptions written up to help you recover sooner."

Shen Weici blinked away her tears: "I've troubled Second Madam."

Madam Wen patted the back of Shen Weici's cold hand: "It is nothing at all. I'll take my leave now — just focus on getting well."

Shen Weici bit her lip and nodded in silence.

The maidservants of Linchun Courtyard all sent Madam Wen out respectfully. The moment she was gone, Yuedeng couldn't wait to lift the curtain and come sit at the head of Shen Weici's bed: "Miss, how did you know the Second Madam would come?"

The tears in Shen Weici's eyes were already gone, leaving only a faint lingering dampness glimmering in the light.

She lay on her side, her cheek resting on her arm, and looked at Yuedeng: "Since yesterday's return from the Zhang estate, the Second Madam's attitude toward me has changed considerably. Unless I'm wrong, she shouldn't give me too much trouble for a while."

"The charcoal and firewood that Linchun Courtyard lacks can be replenished now, while the opportunity is here — and without spending our own money. After all, I can't have the girls in this courtyard freezing alongside me."

"The money we pawned the fur for we'll keep for now. It might come in useful later on, so at least we won't be too short."

Yuedeng asked curiously: "Why won't the Second Madam give Miss trouble for a while?"

Shen Weici glanced at Yuedeng, then lowered her eyes again: "I can't tell you that just yet — I'm afraid it will worry you. Now that the Second Madam has come in person, I'm more than half certain my guess is right. In time you'll come to understand it on your own."

She said this and closed her eyes: "Truth be told, I'd actually feel calmer if she hadn't come."

"But so be it. Nothing comes without strings attached."

Seeing that Shen Weici wouldn't explain further, Yuedeng didn't push, and went instead to tuck the quilt more snugly around her: "Miss, don't keep thinking about it. It's still early — sleep a little more."

Though Shen Weici couldn't truly fall back asleep, she had to wait until the estate physician arrived before she could properly get up.

She turned over and closed her eyes.

By the time dawn broke and the estate physician came to take her pulse, Shen Weici extended her hand through the curtain. She listened to the physician's questions from outside the screen and answered them one by one.

In the end, the physician wrote up a prescription for a wind-cold illness and told the maidservants to accompany him in collecting the medicine.

Not long afterward, a matron sent by the Second Madam arrived with two maidservants. Yuedeng went out to receive them and saw that the Second Madam had sent not only thirty jin of charcoal but also a silver-gilt hand warmer with a flying flower pattern, a forehead wrap, and a winter hat — all things needed for the cold season.

Yuedeng accepted everything with great enthusiasm and couldn't stop offering thanks.

These items were, in truth, hardly significant to Madam Wen. But she had come in person to Linchun Courtyard that day, and seen how desolate the place was, and concluded that things had gone a bit too far. She worried Shen Weici might nurse a grudge and, once married to Zhang Tingyi, use him to turn against her. So she had given a little. Though Shen Weici likely couldn't make much of a stir, earning a measure of her gratitude was still better.

The matron had shed the haughtiness she usually wore, and even managed a smile, politely offering a few courteous words. She asked after Shen Weici's health, gave over the items, and then led the maidservants away.

As soon as she was gone, Yuedeng hurried to have the girls bring in a charcoal brazier and get two fires going, then carried the hand warmer, winter hat, and all the rest inside the curtain and presented them to Shen Weici: "Miss, do you think we can use all these things the Second Madam sent? Isn't it a bit strange that she's suddenly being so nice to us?"

Shen Weici glanced at the items in Yuedeng's hands and looked away: "It's fine. To her, these aren't particularly precious things."

Yuedeng examined the silver-gilt flying flower hand warmer: "This looks quite delicate — surely it must be a fine piece?"

Shen Weici gave a quiet smile, then propped herself up to sit, and asked Yuedeng to bring her needlework and the garment she hadn't finished sewing.

Yuedeng looked at Shen Weici, who was no longer coughing, and couldn't help but ask: "Miss, were you really pretending to be sick just now?"

Shen Weici smiled, tugged the corner of the quilt without a word.

That afternoon, a page boy came from Tingzhu Hall to relay the message: the Second Master had returned, and Shen Weici was summoned to Tingzhu Hall.

Shen Weici had been half-expecting this. She was already presentable and ready to go. Before she left, she caught a glimpse of herself in the mirror and paused, then sat back down at her dressing table and asked Yuedeng to bring the little box that Zhang Yuanheng had sent her last time.

Yuedeng went and fetched the box. Shen Weici looked through the contents and took out the pair of earrings Zhang Yuanheng had given her.

They were a lovely shade of celadon-blue. Shen Weici put them on, watching herself in the mirror, and only then told Yuedeng to come along.

When they arrived at Tingzhu Hall and were shown inside by the page boy, she found Zhang Yuanheng already seated inside, chatting with Shen Rongshen. Shen Rongshen smiled and beckoned Shen Weici over: "Young Master Zhang has made a special trip to see how your calligraphy has progressed over all these days of practice. You must write well for him."

Shen Weici pressed her lips into a smile: "Your daughter looks forward to Young Master Zhang's guidance."

Shen Rongshen nodded approvingly, quite satisfied with this daughter of his — steady without being small-spirited. Zhang Yuanheng and Shen Weici exchanged a glance, and it was Zhang Yuanheng who moved first, going to the desk to smooth out the paper for her to write.

Shen Rongshen looked on at the two of them with a gratified smile.

After writing for a while, Zhang Yuanheng turned his head and glanced at the shy profile of Shen Weici's face, then turned back to Shen Rongshen with a bow: "I find it a bit stifling sitting here writing. May I take Shen Third Miss for a walk around the courtyard?"

Shen Rongshen had long since come to regard Zhang Yuanheng as a promising son-in-law — and Zhang Yuanheng had even mentioned something earlier about coming to formally propose in due course. After that, Shen Rongshen had no desire to constrain the two of them at all. He thought it would do them good to have a quiet conversation alone.

He immediately smiled and said: "Of course."

Zhang Yuanheng felt a release of tension, then turned to Shen Weici: "Would Third Miss be willing to come?"

Shen Weici gave Zhang Yuanheng a quick glance, then lowered her eyes and nodded gently.

No one else caught that brief, fleeting look she had given him — only Zhang Yuanheng himself could feel what it had stirred. Suffice it to say, his heart gave two involuntary leaps and even his capacity for thought temporarily deserted him.

He recovered, stepped aside slightly, and bowed with perfect courtesy, his expression carrying a restrained smile as he said: "Please, Third Miss, lead the way."

Shen Weici looked at the attentive and considerate Zhang Yuanheng beside her, gave a quiet "mm," and walked ahead.

chapters.title: Then I Will Wait for Young Master Zhang
chapters.content:
The two of them went out and made their way toward the more secluded plum forest.

They did not walk side by side on the path — Zhang Yuanheng was ahead, Shen Weici behind, with their respective attendants following at the rear.

In the afternoon, the garden was almost empty. The winter cold kept things quiet, and the grounds were peaceful. When Shen Weici noticed an arbor beside a plum tree ahead, she suggested they sit there for a while.

Zhang Yuanheng had had the same thought. They walked the whole way without managing to exchange a single word — he had only been able to steal occasional glances back, catching glimpses of that jade-green hem trailing behind her.

The two of them sat in the arbor. The attendants waited outside, so they weren't truly alone.

Zhang Yuanheng watched Shen Weici seat herself some seven or eight paces away, her hands resting on her knees, her body turned slightly sideways as she leaned against the railing and looked at the plum blossoms peeking through. He envied every inch of space between her and the arbor rail, wishing he could become the silk handkerchief on her fingers.

He also noticed that she was wearing the earrings he had given her, swaying gently against her face of white jade. Something warm stirred inside him.

He cleared his throat, and with some degree of restrained delicacy, offered a quiet laugh and began: "I never imagined that Third Miss would write to ask me to come of my own accord and help guide Third Miss's calligraphy."

"And that she wished to speak with me privately."

He smiled with some amusement: "I had originally thought Shen Third Miss had no interest in me coming to find her."

Only then did Shen Weici turn her eyes to Zhang Yuanheng's face. She pressed her lips into a faint smile, then said quietly: "Young Master Zhang, two nights ago I had a dream. Would Young Master Zhang like to hear it?"

Zhang Yuanheng heard her put it this way, and replied: "I would be glad to hear it in full, Third Miss."

Shen Weici tilted her head slightly. Her wide sleeves with their delicate sparrow embroidery swept along the railing as she gazed out at the first red plum blossoms and spoke softly: "Ever since Young Master Zhang's letter came, inviting me to view the snow on Chunshan, I have kept it in my heart."

"I have never seen a snowy mountain landscape before, and I have always wondered what it looks like."

"That night, I dreamed that I and Young Master Zhang stood upon a high terrace on Chunshan — white stretched in every direction before our eyes, snowflakes falling one after another in an expanse without end, as though in all the world there were only the two of us."

"But in the very next moment, a hundred people surged up from below the terrace and pointed at us in accusation. Of course they did — you and I had no matchmaker, no betrothal gifts. Naturally we would be talked about."

"I woke up that morning in a start, my heart hammering, frightened by the dream."

Shen Weici looked at Zhang Yuanheng: "Young Master Zhang, you may not understand my heart, but I was truly frightened by that dream."

Zhang Yuanheng, hearing this and seeing those misty, rain-soft eyes of hers, could not help but rise to his feet and take a step toward her: "Third Miss, how could I not understand? I know it is hard for a woman. It was entirely my fault — I did not think this through carefully enough."

He gave her a deep bow of apology: "I have been writing to Third Miss day after day without proper consideration. Between us there is indeed no matchmaker and no betrothal gifts. If you are spoken ill of, the fault lies entirely with me."

"Today I will speak with my father. Even if my mother has not yet returned, I will see to it that a matchmaker comes to your door within these two days. After that, when I invite Third Miss to view the snow on Chunshan, no one will have a word to say."

Song Zhang stood on a distant upper floor, his expression dark, watching this scene below — watching Zhang Yuanheng before Shen Weici, like a puppy eager to hand over his heart, and he gave a cold sneer.

Though he hadn't caught all of their conversation, the besotted look on Zhang Yuanheng's face was enough to make Song Zhang roll his eyes.

He had seen through Shen Weici's tactics clearly enough: she had been the one who took the initiative to invite him in the letter, yet here she sat, keeping her distance and tugging at Zhang Yuanheng's heartstrings, and then spoke in that softly wronged tone, drawing him close with coy reluctance until Zhang Yuanheng was utterly dizzy. Song Zhang imagined that if he were told to die for Shen Weici right now, he probably actually would.

Song Zhang stood with a grim expression watching Shen Weici below, his eyes growing colder still as he observed her faint blush in Zhang Yuanheng's presence. Beside him, Minghé wore an expression of resignation.

These days, his general had brushed off all his social obligations, even declined an imperial invitation, and was coming to the Marquis's estate at all hours, asking him to do all manner of underhanded tasks, and was now spying from behind on other people's conversation.

How was this any different from those idle, dissolute young heirs of powerful families in the capital?

Clearly despising her on the surface, yet keeping watch over the Third Miss day after day — and she had never once provoked him on her own. Whatever the case, she was part of the Second Branch of this Marquis household, and the general was so occupied of late. How did he have the energy for this sort of thing?

Here below, Shen Weici saw Zhang Yuanheng bow in apology and quickly rose, reaching to support him at the arm, then swiftly withdrew her hand. She looked up at him: "Weici's origins are humble, and I should never have dared speak of this to Young Master Zhang. But my difficulty lies in having no one to lean on, an uncertain future — and yet my heart has already placed its trust in Young Master Zhang. That is why I told him of my dream."

"If Young Master Zhang can come to propose soon and settle the betrothal, that would naturally be best. But if Young Master Zhang faces difficulties, how could Weici possibly press him?"

Zhang Yuanheng's heart grew ever more tender at her words. He spoke quietly in return: "There are no difficulties at all. My heart has already decided on Third Miss. Though she is concubine-born, she has a quality of noble refinement, a rare intelligence and clarity — I saw that in her from the first glance."

"And since Master Shen also favors our match, it could not be better. How could I delay further? Third Miss need only wait for my news — a matchmaker will certainly come within these two days."
