Shen Weici blinked in surprise, and when she raised her eyes, Song Zhang's face was bent close — his posture completely relaxed, both legs spread, one hand braced on his knee, his sword at his belt pressing against her leg, his boot almost touching her embroidered shoe.

Yet his expression was utterly detached — brow faintly raised, impossible to tell whether he was pleased or not.

And the scent of him was so close, and the pressure of that tall frame bearing down on her so palpable, that Shen Weici found it oddly difficult to breathe.

She leaned back just slightly, then shook her head. "Young Master Song's bearing is too striking. I simply don't dare to look directly."

Song Zhang heard this and could not suppress a short, scoffing sound. "Don't dare to look, or don't want to look?"

Shen Weici was not entirely sure what Song Zhang was getting at. She had been raised from childhood on the Women's Rules, which stated that women were not to look directly at men — not even close male relatives. She had made a habit of averting her gaze, and her phrasing just now had been her way of expressing this — clearly he had not followed her meaning.

She paused, then continued to avoid Song Zhang's pressing eyes, and said quietly: "What does it matter to Young Master Song whether I look at him or not?"

"I am only keeping to propriety. I ask that Young Master Song not make things difficult for me."

Song Zhang's expression darkened. "Keeping to propriety? I've seen how bold you were when looking at Zhang Yuanheng."

Shen Weici finally looked at Song Zhang. "Why does Young Master Song keep bringing up Master Zhang?"

"Master Zhang was the match my father arranged for me. Before, I had intended with all sincerity to marry him — naturally it was different from anyone else."

Shen Weici's phrase — anyone else — struck Song Zhang somewhere in his chest like a small, sharp point. He felt, abruptly, no different from the men who went fawning after women to earn their regard.

Hadn't his helping Shen Weici been, in part, wanting to earn a place in her heart?

He had become the very sort of man he looked down upon.

And the woman he could not stop putting himself forward for was one who was practiced in drawing men in. What was he thinking, diminishing himself like this?

His fingers curled against his side. The sour, out-of-sorts feeling was not something he could let show — if he did, Shen Weici would know she had gotten to him, and she would feel satisfied.

Back there in his quarters for those few days, he had even been talking himself into accepting that he had some feeling for her. Had convinced himself it was all right.

Now he only wanted to regret that he had been too accommodating with Shen Weici. He had helped her, and she accepted it as though it were simply her due.

chapters.title: Not Entirely Heartless
chapters.content:
Song Zhang rose with a dark expression and was about to leave when his sleeve was caught. He paused slightly — and saw that Shen Weici, who had been seated, had also risen. She stood before him, face bare of powder or rouge, quiet as a painting of spring hills.

She gave him a proper, graceful bow: "Young Lord Song has helped me, and Weici holds that deep in her heart. Right now Weici is lowly and without influence, and has nothing to offer in return."

"But if Young Lord Song should ever need Weici to do anything in the future, Weici will certainly be willing — she will not refuse."

As she said this, those eyes — like the clear water of an autumn lotus pond, like moonlight over snow — looked toward him.

Song Zhang held Shen Weici's gaze and felt the tightness in his chest ease a fraction. At least she had a conscience. She was not entirely heartless.

The irritation in him dispersed slightly. He arched an eyebrow at her: "You would agree to anything I say?"

Shen Weici paused, then nodded: "As long as it is within what I am able to do."

Song Zhang curved his lips: "Then I shall have to think carefully."

With that he looked at Shen Weici once more — a long, deep look — and walked away in long strides.

At the far end of the water pavilion corridor, Shen Zhaozhao had seen every moment of this scene. The embroidered handkerchief in her fingers was twisted tight, and she ground her teeth.

She now suspected that Shen Weici must have been secretly seducing Song Zhang, and that Song Zhang was helping her from behind the scenes because of it.

She had truly underestimated Shen Weici — that even Song Zhang could be seduced by her.

She looked once more at Shen Weici's figure, then turned and left in fury.

Back in Linchun Courtyard, Shen Weici stood by the window and quietly went over everything that had happened since coming to the Marquis Manor, turning each incident over in her mind one more time — then sat back at her writing table to copy.

In the candlelight, Shen Weici's figure was slender and composed. She held the brush and wrote each stroke with care. Yuedeng, watching beside her, could not help but say: "What is the use of making the characters this beautiful, Miss?"

"Fifty pages — does the Old Madam really look closely? At most she will give it a quick glance and that is that."

Shen Weici had long since made a habit of doing everything as properly as she could, and replied quietly: "I only need, within the limits of what I can do, to give no one a single crack to find fault with."

"Even if she only glances at it, I will not leave anything that gives others a handle over me."

With that she pressed the embroidery frame into Yuedeng's hands: "Your needlework was taught by me personally. I have already sketched the pattern for you — later I want to see how you have done."

Yuedeng, caught off guard as something was thrust into her hands, settled down obediently and sat beside Shen Weici to work on the stitching.

The next day, Shen Weici rose early. She put on the lined jacket she had chosen from Lady Wen's fabric — a white ground with a sparrow-and-flower pattern that suited her complexion well. It lacked the tender, warm allure of the rose-pink, but carried instead a kind of cool, still beauty all its own.

Shen Weici lingered at the mirror a little longer than usual. She pinned a jade hairpin in her hair, put on earrings, used a little of the face powder Lady Wen had bought for her previously, and applied a thin layer of rouge to her lips.

The face was already alluring by nature. With the touch of rouge, it was more vivid still.

Yuedeng still wanted to press a flower mark onto Shen Weici's forehead, but Shen Weici stopped her: "I am wearing a little color today because we are going to meet the Earl's Manor elders, and being too plain would not give a good impression. But being too heavily made up would also make a poor one."

"I will only wear the one layer of rouge to give myself a little color — it may be more pleasing that way."

Yuedeng accepted this with some regret.

She still remembered the Flower Festival two years ago, when she had pressed a tiny cinnabar plum blossom on the young mistress's forehead and drawn the eyes of the whole crowd — people had all exclaimed she looked like a goddess descended from the heavens.

The jacket had a half-high collar with a ring of silver squirrel fur at the neckline — quite warm.

When Shen Weici went to the Second Branch, her father and Lady Wen were inside.

Hearing her father giving Lady Wen instructions for the visit to the Earl's Manor, she quietly took a seat to one side.

Shen Zhaozhao, sitting beside her, looked Shen Weici up and down coldly, noting the hairpin in her hair — one of the ones Shen Zhaozhao herself had given her — and the earrings, also from her. Things she had long since grown tired of and did not wear, and yet on Shen Weici they looked striking.

She also recalled the scene that afternoon before, when Song Zhang had walked over to Shen Weici of his own accord and bent close to speak with her. Just thinking of it made the anger rise in her chest.

She was still the legitimate daughter of this Marquis Manor. Song Zhang had never once taken the initiative to speak with her, and even when she approached him first, he barely acknowledged her. Why was he the one seeking out Shen Weici?

She looked again at Shen Weici's appearance today — clearly she had put in more effort than her usual plainness.

She gave a cold snort: "You haven't even married into the Earl's Manor yet and you're already this calculating. If they take a dislike to you when you visit, just see what face you'll have left."

"Though I suppose for someone like you, an Earl's Manor that is practically in decline already is still a step up. I suppose it does take some effort."

Shen Weici made no reply. She held her warm teacup with both hands and took a quiet sip.

Shen Rongshen overhead this and could not help but frown in reprimand: "Do not speak of your sister that way."

"Don't you know what is being said about you outside? For the two of you sisters to be on good terms is the only way this branch will have any peace. If you keep targeting your younger sister like this, do not bother coming to pay your respects anymore — you can simply stay in your own courtyard."

Shen Zhaozhao was taken aback. She looked at her father with wounded eyes: "I didn't say anything wrong. The Earl's Manor match is a step up for her — what did I say that was incorrect?"

Shen Rongshen's brow deepened: "Weici is a daughter of the Marquis Manor. Even as a concubine-born, she carries the Marquis Manor's standing. Marrying into the Yiyong Earl's Manor is not a step up for her."

"To say so is to slap the Marquis Manor's own face."

Shen Zhaozhao's face went slowly pale and then tight with a fierce look: "She is an illegitimate daughter born outside. Her mother never once set foot in this Manor. What right does she have to call herself a daughter of the Marquis Manor?"

"You only made a show of raising her so that she could marry Zhang Tingyi…"

Shen Zhaozhao's words were cut off sharply by Shen Rongshen: "Be quiet. If you do not change this temper of yours, you will have plenty of suffering ahead of you."

"What has Weici done to you since she came? Why can you not tolerate her?"

"Her marrying into the Yiyong Earl's Manor is also of benefit to this household. If you continue making a scene, get out of my sight right now."

Shen Rongshen finished speaking, swept his sleeve, and walked straight out.

Shen Zhaozhao's mind went blank. Since Shen Weici had arrived, her father had not been as warm and easy with her as before, and had scolded her in front of servants several times.

She had not said anything wrong — so why was her father this angry?

Tears fell blankly, then she threw herself into Lady Wen's arms and wept openly.

"Mother, Father scolded me again because of that wretched woman. What have I even said wrong?"

Lady Wen stroked Shen Zhaozhao's back and said in a low, soothing voice: "Your father has been demoted in office and is vexed these days. Say less and stop putting yourself in his way."

Shen Zhaozhao raised her tearful eyes to Lady Wen: "But I didn't say anything wrong — why is Father defending her like this?"

Lady Wen shot a quick glance at Shen Weici and said quietly: "With the rumors outside affecting your reputation as well, you should keep a lower profile for now. Rein in your temper. After the new year when you marry, that will be all — what is there to be angry about? I am still here at home."

She called a matron over: "Take Second Young Miss back first and look after her. I will come and check on her shortly."

The matron went to Shen Zhaozhao and coaxed and reassured until she was able to take her out.

Only then did Lady Wen turn her gaze to Shen Weici.

Shen Weici was still holding her teacup with the same composure, as though everything that had just taken place had nothing to do with her. Whatever one might say, this steadiness of hers truly was something Lady Wen had not expected. Perhaps she was not as obedient and fragile as she appeared on the surface.

Lady Wen looked at her with unhurried ease: "Your father sent a card to the Yiyong Earl's Manor yesterday. Today we will take you there this morning. Are you ready?"

Shen Weici looked at Lady Wen and nodded: "All prepared."

Lady Wen's expression remained cool: "This visit is to discuss your engagement to Zhang Erlang. Whether it succeeds or not depends entirely on what impression you leave at the Earl's Manor."

Lady Wen's words pushed every possible outcome onto her shoulders, framing the match — which should properly be managed by the parents — as though it were entirely Shen Weici's own affair to conduct, as though she herself had no intention of being involved.

Shen Weici understood perfectly well that Lady Wen could not bear to see her married well, and only lowered her eyes in silence.

chapters.title: Visiting the Earl's Manor to Discuss the Match
chapters.content:
They returned from breakfast and tidied up, and when the matron from the Second Branch came to summon her, Shen Weici went with Yuedeng.

At the front gate, Lady Wen was already waiting in the carriage. Seeing Shen Weici board after her, she seemed somewhat impatient and called to the coachman to set off.

Inside the carriage, Lady Wen did not say a single word to Shen Weici — not about the Manor's etiquette or conduct, not how to address the family or what to say. Shen Weici quietly went over everything in her own mind, avoiding any possibility of a misstep.

She also felt, quietly, a certain nervousness. This was her first time meeting Zhang Yuanheng's parents.

But the fact that the Earl's Manor had sent a reply proved that this marriage could still be discussed. Shen Weici was also determined to make a good impression on the Zhang family elders.

The carriage soon arrived at the gate of the Yiyong Earl's Manor, where a servant was already waiting and came forward at once to receive them.

Shen Weici followed behind Lady Wen as they descended and went in through the front gate with the steward.

This was her first time coming to the Yiyong Earl's Manor. It would not do to look around too freely, so she walked quietly and properly behind Lady Wen.

They had not yet reached the front hall when a young man's voice came: "Second Lady Shen."

"My father was afraid the steward might not see to everything properly, so he sent me to welcome you."

Shen Weici looked up at the sound of the voice and saw Zhang Yuanheng standing before Lady Wen, in a bamboo-green round-collar long robe — refined, elegant, with a smile in his eyes.

His glance also flicked briefly toward Shen Weici, but was pulled back with disciplined restraint.

Though inwardly Zhang Yuanheng's heart beat twice of its own accord. That single glance at Shen Weici told him she looked subtly different today from before — he could see she had worn a touch of rouge, and she was captivating.

Lady Wen, seeing Zhang Yuanheng come to meet them in person, understood exactly what this was about and smiled, telling him to lead the way.

On the way, Lady Wen asked: "It is not a rest day today — are you not on duty at the palace?"

Zhang Yuanheng replied with proper courtesy: "Last night I saw the card the Marquis Manor sent, so I arranged with a colleague to swap our shift. I stayed especially to be here at home — it seemed more respectful."

Lady Wen heard this. Zhang Yuanheng had indeed put thought into it, and by his expression he was quite drawn to Shen Weici.

Lady Wen smiled faintly and said no more.

Shen Weici glanced at Zhang Yuanheng's back from time to time, and hearing that he had traded shifts to stay home, felt her heart settle a little more.

They soon arrived at the front hall. Lord and Lady Zhang caught sight of Lady Wen bringing Shen Weici in, took a quick look at Shen Weici, and rose to exchange pleasantries with Lady Wen.

They had heard the talk outside and knew the whole story. Though they had a very poor opinion of Lady Wen's kind of conduct — no household with any dignity would treat a concubine-born daughter in such a way, with not a shred of noble bearing — they still greeted her with smiles at the surface.

After a round of pleasantries, Shen Weici came forward and paid her respects to Lord and Lady Zhang. Her movements were proper without being constricted, and once she had risen, she took a small sachet from her sleeve and placed it in Lady Zhang's hands: "Last time I heard from Young Master Zhang that Lady Zhang had tired from the journey back to the capital. I made this calming sachet here — the embroidery on it was done in my spare time. The herbs inside are ones that help with sleep. Sleep well, and your spirits will be better too."

The sachet had been bought a few nights before when Shen Weici had sent the gate boy Laifu out on the errand. In the past, her mother's lung illness had made nights difficult — she would cough herself awake and then be unable to sleep again, and slowly her health had worn thin and her hair had begun to fall.

Shen Weici had been anxious and worried. Hearing that calming fragrances helped with sleep, she had read through many books on compounding scents, and since there was no money to buy what she needed, she had gone into the hills herself to gather herbs and flowers.

The blends she made proved useful, and her mother was able to sleep more peacefully through the nights.

Lady Lin took the sachet Shen Weici had placed in her hands and paused. The embroidery on it was exquisitely fine — a lifelike peony and butterfly, symbolizing prosperity and long life.

She brought it to her nose: the scent was light and elegant, neither too strong nor too faint, and distinctly pleasing. She looked up at Shen Weici's face.

She had not had a particularly high opinion of Shen Weici to begin with.

Though the Earl's Manor had fallen to the bottom tier of the capital's families by now, their ancestral lands, shops, and estates were still considerable, and the household was well-off even without official service. And her own son had placed in the imperial examinations through merit, had earned the Emperor's praise, and was young and full of promise — he could certainly have matched someone from a respectable established family.

The Jian'an Marquis Manor was a step above the Earl's Manor in rank, and both Second Lord Shen and First Lord Shen held official positions at court, and Princess Consort Huimin was in the First Branch — but Shen Weici's mother was gone, she had not grown up in the capital, and there had been that coughing of blood — her constitution was probably poor. Inwardly Lady Lin was not very satisfied.

If not for her own son threatening to resign his post and then going to the Song Ducal Manor to personally make amends, they would not have been willing to see the Marquis Manor at all.

But now, looking at Shen Weici's gentle brow and eyes, the fineness of her needlework, the soft and measured way she spoke, the propriety and bearing that were correct in every particular — and a face that was beautiful to the point of being almost unnatural — it was no wonder her son could not stop thinking about her.

Still, the sachet showed some understanding of what was appropriate, and it did earn Lady Lin a degree of warmth toward her. A smile came to her face: "Good child — you went to this trouble for me."

Lady Wen, watching from the side, thought to herself that she had truly underestimated Shen Weici. Who knew she had such tricks for winning over elders? She had never sent any such sachet to her.

She kept the cold amusement inward and said to Lady Lin: "There was some misunderstanding between our families before. My husband specifically asked me to come today and set things right — shall we sit down and speak?"

Lady Lin smiled: "Of course."

She called for a maid to bring tea and settled into her seat.

Lady Wen spoke with Lady Lin — the usual roundabout talk about misunderstandings and the like — while Shen Weici sat quietly beside Lady Wen with her eyes slightly downcast, both hands folded properly at her knees.

Zhang Yuanheng, seated across the room, kept letting his gaze drift to Shen Weici. His thoughts wandered and he desperately wanted to go and speak with her.

He had not seen her in many days. She looked a little thinner, and concern for her stirred in his heart again.

Thinking of how she had just given his mother the sachet, a warmth rose inside him without cause — so warm he felt his eyes grow hot.

He could not wait any longer. He wanted to tell her every bit of the misunderstanding from these past days, and could not bear for her to hold even a fraction of it against him.

He rose from his seat, walked to Lady Wen, and folded his hands in a bow: "I hear Third Young Miss Shen has not yet fully recovered. The front hall does not have enough charcoal warmth and I am afraid the cold air may trouble her. Shall I let a maid take Third Young Miss to the warm room to rest a while?"

Lady Wen stiffened, but with everyone in the room looking at her, refusing to let Shen Weici go would not do — she had already earned a name outside for mistreating her concubine-born daughter, and so she had no choice but to put on an expression of warmth and say: "Zhang Erlang is considerate as always. Your constitution is not yet fully recovered — go with the maid to the warm room and rest. If anything is needed, I will send someone to fetch you."

Though Shen Weici would have preferred to stay and listen to how Lady Wen spoke, so she could know how to respond, Lady Wen had spoken, and she had no choice. She set down her teacup, rose, thanked Lady Wen, and made her farewells to Lord and Lady Zhang in the room.

Then she looked once at Zhang Yuanheng, and said softly: "Thank you also, Young Master Zhang, for your consideration."

chapters.title: Unable to Bear Failing Her
chapters.content:
That one voice from Shen Weici — clear and melodious as a warbler — stopped Zhang Yuanheng's heart in its tracks.

And when she lifted her eyes — lovely and subtle as the color of mountain lake water, rippling with light — all his thoughts scattered at once, and he even forgot what she had just said.

Lord Zhang, watching his son make a fool of himself in front of the Third Young Miss Shen, was nearly beside himself with exasperation.

The boy had dared to offend the Song Ducal Manor over this woman — he was truly bewitched. There was nothing to be done with him.

He gave a cough and called a maid over with a frown to lead the way.

Shen Weici, seeing the maid come to her side, did not look toward Zhang Yuanheng again and followed the maid out.

Zhang Yuanheng watched Shen Weici's retreating figure in a daze, breathing in the lingering scent she left behind. His heart had already gone with her.

He then heard Lady Wen speak of the matter of the marriage to Zhang Tingyi — all of it blamed on the Zhang household's pressure, identical to what Lord Zhang had said previously.

Any discerning person could see the truth of those words. His only worry was that his father might not follow the narrative, making things awkward for both parties.

He looked at his father, his expression carrying a firmness the likes of which had never been there before.

Lord Zhang, reading his son's expression, knew his meaning. Zhang Yuanheng had come to his room the night before, once the card from the Marquis Manor arrived, and had stayed for a full hour.

He was tired of it all now. He had given in completely and had no heart left to argue with his own son.

That stubborn streak — who on earth had he inherited it from? Threatening to resign his post and refusing to budge a single inch.

He had laid out all the consequences plainly: offend the Song Ducal Manor and things would be difficult enough in the official world that resigning or not would amount to the same thing — he could bear all consequences himself.

And Zhang Yuanheng had said: he would bear them.

Lord Zhang had capitulated.

Such was fate. He had no choice but to accept it.

He glanced at Zhang Yuanheng and smiled: "Second Lady Shen is too kind. We had no other intentions to begin with."

"Now that the matter is resolved, it is also a good thing. We also know the Marquis Manor would never have done anything of that sort — the rumors outside were simply people talking nonsense."

Lady Wen's expression flickered. She forced a smile.

Zhang Yuanheng, hearing this, finally felt at ease inwardly. With his thoughts fixed on going to explain everything to Shen Weici, he rose from his seat and withdrew.

He went to the warm room. The maid was about to announce his arrival, but he quickly stopped her, stepped quietly to the curtain and lifted it — and found Shen Weici turned slightly to one side, bending slightly to play with a cat that had come to her feet.

Her long, pale fingers stroked the cat's fur gently, a soft smile in her eyes. Then she extended a fingertip to tease the cat's nose.

Strands of hair had fallen loose, her jade hairpin catching the light with a soft glow. A figure of pure jade and bright flowers — anyone who looked could not look away. The maids in the room had already had their attention drawn entirely to that warm and beautiful person.

Zhang Yuanheng felt something go soft in his heart. He stepped inside, bent to pick up the cat at Shen Weici's feet, and placed it in her arms with a smile: "This is a Persian cat. She is very gentle and loves to be held. The more you pet her, the more she will take to you."

Shen Weici heard Zhang Yuanheng and, with the cat in her arms, found herself unable to resist the urge to pet its head. The Persian cat closed its eyes as if in bliss, purring softly as she buried her head in Shen Weici's arms, not moving an inch — round and adorable in a most endearing way.

Shen Weici could not suppress the smile that came to the corner of her lips. She was completely charmed.

Zhang Yuanheng's gaze had never left Shen Weici. Seeing her smile, he found a smile of his own rising on his face. He sat beside Shen Weici and let his gaze rest on her face: "I broke my promise last time. Was Third Young Miss Shen angry with me?"

Shen Weici paused. She looked toward Zhang Yuanheng and saw his eyes were full of remorse. She smiled gently: "I do not blame Young Master Zhang. I understand he also had his difficulties."

Zhang Yuanheng looked at Shen Weici's smile, and with a kind of smitten directness began: "The day before I had planned to come and propose, the Second Lord of the Song Ducal Manor suddenly sent someone to my father to say they wished to arrange a marriage."

"The Song Ducal Manor is a grand and powerful household, far above the Yiyong Earl's Manor in standing. And our Earl's Manor has been declining with each generation — though our ancestors once produced a Prime Minister, none of my father's generation of uncles have entered official service. They all went to various places to engage in trade."

"My father alone is keeping the Earl's Manor going. My elder brother has been sickly since birth and stays home to recover; my elder sister is already married; of the family, only I am in official service. My father placed all his hopes on me, believing that an alliance with the Song Ducal Manor would allow the Earl's Manor to flourish again."

"But I have never wanted to live by clinging to the powerful. I only want to spend my days with the person who holds my heart."

"Afterward I went to find Third Young Miss Shen twice, but I was turned away by Lord Shen. The gate boy would not take my letters either. I was filled with anxiety."

"I have only recently been able to persuade my family, and I have also gone in person to the Song Ducal Manor to make my apologies."

"I intend to marry only you, and I will not break my word again. I hope Third Young Miss Shen will not be disheartened — my feelings have never changed."

This earnest and heartfelt account made clear to Shen Weici exactly why Zhang Yuanheng had missed his moment.

She did not know quite what she felt. She was moved by his steadfast devotion, and also felt sorrow for him.

He should have had a much more promising future. She had nothing to offer him.

She asked quietly: "You have offended the Song Ducal Manor — are you not afraid they will make things difficult for you in the future?"

Zhang Yuanheng smiled: "I have already made my apologies to the Song Ducal Manor's Second Lord. We work in the same department. He values my abilities and did not hold it heavily against me — in fact, he praised my courage. It may even have worked in my favor."

He looked at Shen Weici: "But if I truly am demoted one day because of this, would you still be willing to marry me?"

Shen Weici's eyes held a trace of sadness: "I am marrying Young Master Zhang himself — not your official rank."

"What I seek is simply a stable and settled life. I have never competed with anyone for wealth or status."

"I would not leave because Young Master Zhang was demoted."

She lowered her eyes: "It is only that Young Master Zhang had such a bright future ahead of him. If this matter truly damages your standing at the Song Ducal Manor and affects your career, my conscience is troubled. I feel I am not worth it."

Zhang Yuanheng said quickly: "I have no great ambitions to begin with. What I seek is the same as Third Young Miss Shen."

"I feel Third Young Miss Shen is the most precious thing in my heart — more precious than anything else. She is worth it."

Shen Weici went still, her eyes growing faintly red. She blinked a few times. Besides her mother and Yuedeng, it had been a very long time since anyone had treasured her like this.

Perhaps Zhang Yuanheng would be the companion of her lifetime — she would follow him step by step, be the devoted wife at his side, spare him any trouble in the inner household. It was the only thing she could do for him.

Shen Weici stroked the Persian cat in her arms again with her fingertips, bit the corner of her lip, and after a long pause said in a low voice: "Thank you."

Zhang Yuanheng heard that hushed voice, and also sat looking at Shen Weici in a trance. He looked at her eyes — fine as gentle waves, white and clear and luminous — like a flawless piece of beautiful jade. Being near her made his heart feel warm.

She deserved to be cherished and well protected. He was willing to devote the rest of his life to being her shelter against all wind and rain, to ensure she never suffered another grievance.

He understood the hardships she had endured in the Marquis Manor. He had heard all the rumors, and that was when he had finally understood how difficult things had been for her.

That was why he could not bring himself to fail her.

chapters.title: He Wished He Could Marry Her Tomorrow
chapters.content:
The morning light was mild and gentle, and the glow filtering through the pale yellow window paper was softer still.

Even in the cold of winter, sitting inside the warm room with a purring, contented cat nestled in her arms, Shen Weici had not felt this relaxed and at ease in many long years.

She knew Zhang Yuanheng's eyes were on her. She let a shy warmth come into her own, a smile playing at her lips, and with her fingertip she pinched the Persian cat's ear, then spoke softly: "Has Young Master Zhang received the letter I sent?"

Zhang Yuanheng paused, looking at Shen Weici's face — her brows and eyes exquisitely drawn, that smiling expression pressed into his heart: "What letter does Third Young Miss mean?"

He paused: "After the day I last saw Third Young Miss alone, I have not received any letter from her."

Shen Weici's fingers stilled very slightly, then she went back to rubbing the cat's chin. She nodded: "I only asked in passing. The delivery boy must have lost it."

Then she turned her head toward Zhang Yuanheng and drew a small, finely embroidered pouch from her sleeve and held it out: "Young Master Zhang has been so sincere in his feelings toward me. I am deeply grateful. These past days I have had some free time, so I embroidered a pouch. If Young Master Zhang does not find it too humble, please accept it."

Zhang Yuanheng looked down at the pouch in Shen Weici's pale fingers. On it was a vividly embroidered nine-colored deer, a deer carrying good fortune — a beautiful and auspicious design.

He could not help reaching out to take it and study it carefully. The stitches were close and even — only exceptional needlework could produce a design this fine.

He looked again at Shen Weici, at those red lips and bright eyes, the hint of a smile at the corners as she asked: "Does Young Master Zhang like it?"

Zhang Yuanheng felt a warmth rolling behind his eyes that made his fingers tremble slightly. He said with great feeling: "I do."

Shen Weici nodded. She then lowered her head and spoke quietly again: "In ordinary times I also like to blend fragrances. Does Young Master Zhang have any particular scent he prefers? I can blend something and have it sent to you."

In this moment, Zhang Yuanheng felt that to encounter a woman like Shen Weici at his age was the greatest fortune of his life.

She had about her always this calm, orchid-like quality — still and warm at once, without a trace of shallowness or vanity, her soft voice a quiet comfort to the heart.

Even if life in the Marquis Manor had not been easy for her, she had never once brought up her own difficulties with him. He had heard that even her winter charcoal had been withheld by her stepmother — someone as frail as she was, and he dared not imagine how she had managed.

He suppressed his emotion and said quietly: "Whatever fragrance Third Young Miss blends, I will like."

Shen Weici glanced at Zhang Yuanheng, smiled again: "Good."

That one smile made Zhang Yuanheng's throat tighten. Every nerve in him straightened. He wished desperately he could marry her right now and bring her home. He murmured: "What more could a husband ask for, to have a wife like this?"

Shen Weici blinked, then covered her mouth and laughed softly: "We are not even betrothed yet."

Zhang Yuanheng, lost in looking at Shen Weici's playfulness in this moment, said earnestly: "I wish I could marry you tomorrow, Young Miss."

Shen Weici's eyes shifted with a ripple of warmth. She turned her head gently to one side and did not answer.

A maid came in from outside carrying a small tray of sweet pastries and held them before Shen Weici: "Third Young Miss, please have a taste. Our Second Young Master specially asked us to make these for you earlier. When Young Miss — the eldest, before her marriage — was still at home, she loved these too."

"These are plum blossom rice cakes made with fresh-picked plum blossoms. They are best with lotus heart tea. We think you will love them."

Shen Weici caught the faint fragrance of plum blossom and, noticing the maids all looking at her expectantly, took a piece and bit in. The texture was silky and sweet, and a sip of the slightly bitter lotus heart tea brought the flavors into balance — it was genuinely delicious.

She smiled: "It is very good."

Zhang Yuanheng saw that Shen Weici was pleased and felt a gladness rise in him: "I will send some more to you later."

Shen Weici took another small bite and nodded quietly.

The maids, watching Shen Weici eat with such graceful, unhurried elegance — seated there with a luminous glow about her, otherworldly in her beauty, and yet obviously with a gentle temperament — thought to themselves: if she became the young mistress of the Earl's Manor, she would certainly be easy to serve.

The maids exchanged glances as they looked at their Second Young Master's expression watching the Third Young Miss. Not just the Second Young Master — they themselves had been here with Third Young Miss only a short while and already liked her.

Much better than the cousin Miss who had been considered before.

After a little while longer, a matron suddenly pushed in through the curtain from outside: "Third Young Miss, the Second Lady is asking for you in the front hall."

Shen Weici recognized the matron as one of Lady Wen's, acknowledged her, and set the cat in her arms down on the carpet before rising. She glanced at Zhang Yuanheng, lowered her eyes, and followed the maid out with her attendant.

Zhang Yuanheng hurried after her. The moment he stepped out the door, a hand clapped his shoulder from behind: "Is that Third Young Miss Shen?"

Zhang Yuanheng glanced at Shen Weici's retreating back, then turned to look at his elder brother Zhang Mingqing, eyes full of warmth: "Yes."

He heard his elder brother cough twice and said with concern: "It is cold outside, Brother. You caught a cold again a few days ago — please go back inside first."

Zhang Mingqing shook his head: "This marriage of yours — I ought to have a look. Unfortunately I did not catch a proper glimpse just now."

Zhang Yuanheng smiled: "Beautiful beyond comparison — I am the one who is punching above his weight."

Zhang Mingqing raised an eyebrow: "Then I must go and have a proper look."

Zhang Yuanheng had no way to argue. He laughed helplessly: "Come along then."

In the front hall, Shen Weici was already standing beside Lady Wen, who was in conversation with Lady Lin.

Lady Lin was saying: "We also wish to unite our two families. However, Second Lady Shen knows the difficulties of a mother's heart. Let me call again in a few days and we can discuss things in more detail."

Lady Lin smiled: "We are both mothers — I understand completely. Send a card ahead of time and I will be here waiting for you."

They exchanged a few more words, and then Lady Lin accompanied Lady Wen and Shen Weici to see them out.

Zhang Yuanheng came hurrying from behind. Seeing Shen Weici about to leave with her stepmother, his chest tightened. He quickly stepped forward and murmured to Shen Weici: "Could you spare one more word?"

Shen Weici glanced at him: "What is it Young Master Zhang wishes to say?"

Zhang Yuanheng stepped between her and Lady Wen to block Lady Wen's line of sight, pressed a small brocade purse into Shen Weici's hand, and looked at her quietly: "Take this. I know you have difficulties in the Marquis Manor. Do not worry — I will be coming to propose very soon."

Shen Weici closed her fingers around it for a moment and knew at once what it contained. She looked at Zhang Yuanheng and shook her head, then pressed it back into his hand.

She stepped back, gathered her sleeves, and caught from the corner of her eye that Lady Wen's matron was coming around to look. She said quietly: "I have taken note of the recipe for those plum blossom cakes — thank you, Young Master Zhang."

Then she moved back to Lady Wen's side.

Zhang Yuanheng stood looking after her, closing his fingers around what he held.

Zhang Mingqing, standing to one side, had caught a full view of Shen Weici's face and paused slightly — cool skin, flawless features, brows and eyes like a painting. Truly like an immortal.

chapters.title: She Will Not Have an Easy Road
chapters.content:
They were accompanied all the way to the front gate. Watching Shen Weici follow the Second Lady into the carriage, Zhang Yuanheng only then realized that in the fluster he had forgotten to give her the item she had returned to him.

He stood in place, warm and genteel, watching that carriage slowly recede into the distance until even the shape of it was gone, until his elder brother beside him said: "It's out of sight — what are you still looking at?"

Zhang Yuanheng came to himself with a rueful smile and turned anxiously to his mother: "Was Second Lady Shen willing for us to come and propose?"

Lady Lin gathered her sleeves, gave Zhang Yuanheng one look, said nothing, and turned to go inside.

Zhang Yuanheng watched his mother's retreating figure and frowned. He turned quickly to follow.

Meanwhile, inside the carriage, Shen Weici sat quietly. Lady Wen, across from her, had not spoken — and Shen Weici did not ask.

Lady Wen tilted her chin and looked at Shen Weici with cold appraisal, the faintest trace of a cold smile at her lips. A girl from the countryside — an illegitimate daughter — had come into the Marquis Manor to become a daughter of the household, and was now aiming to fly higher and become the young mistress of an Earl's Manor. Such a neat progression of ambitions.

She would not allow this to go so smoothly.

The matter of Zhang Tingyi — she had never believed it could have worked out so conveniently. Her reputation had since been ruined. When the First Lady of Mingyuan Marquis Manor held her banquet, every woman of standing in the capital received an invitation — except her. Had the Third Branch not come to gloat and asked why she had not attended, she might have remained ignorant of it entirely.

She had become the laughingstock of the capital's noble wives — the venomous stepmother who mistreated her concubine-born stepdaughter. A source of gossip over tea. One by one, they had stopped seeking her company.

Her husband had been demoted by two grades as well, and there would be no holding her head up now.

Lady Wen had kept her composure in front of the servants these past days, but her nights were spent in restless torment. The hatred would drive her from sleep in the small hours, and she would lie there burning with it, wishing she could flay Shen Weici alive.

Yet she could not find a single shred of evidence. Shen Weici seemed entirely removed from the affair. There was nowhere for her fury to go.

Lady Wen's gaze was too cold, and Shen Weici had felt it long since.

She knew that after this, she had become a thorn lodged deep in Lady Wen's heart — one that could not be left where it was.

She had used a little calculation on Zhang Yuanheng today, wanting only to make him more resolved to propose quickly. In truth, if it came to a direct confrontation with Lady Wen, she was nowhere near strong enough to win. If Lady Wen was truly determined to deal with her, she could not guard against everything.

She lowered her brow, deep in thought, knowing that the only way was to marry out as soon as possible and break free of Lady Wen's control — only then could she hold her own future in her hands.

The carriage returned to the Jian'an Marquis Manor. Lady Wen stepped down with her matrons without once looking at Shen Weici and walked straight inside.

Yuedeng, following behind Shen Weici, said softly: "How did the talk of the marriage go?"

"The Second Lady's expression does not look pleased — does that mean it went well?"

Shen Weici had never intended to ask Lady Wen about it — she would not be willing to say much to her anyway.

From those last few words she had caught between Lady Wen and Lady Zhang, Shen Weici had already guessed the shape of it. They had not yet come to a full agreement.

But as long as the Earl's Manor had made up their minds to come and propose, Lady Wen could not openly refuse on the surface.

She said nothing. She crossed through the front gate, and as her gaze swept over Laifu standing there, their eyes met. Laifu felt a small flush of guilt and immediately looked down, calling: "Third Young Miss."

Shen Weici pressed her lips into a smile and nodded, pausing in front of him to say warmly: "You went to a lot of trouble running errands for me the other day. When you are free today, come to my courtyard — I have something prepared for you as a token of thanks."

Laifu said at once: "Running errands for Third Young Miss is this servant's duty."

Shen Weici smiled and walked on.

Back in Linchun Courtyard, Shen Weici sat on the low platform and sewed the remaining herbs into a sachet, then asked Yuedeng to take one each to the Old Madam, Lady Wen, and Third Mistress Wang.

One was also sent to Princess Consort Huimin's courtyard — though she was away, the gesture was meant as the same sincerity.

Yuedeng was puzzled: "Miss, why are you sending sachets for no particular reason?"

Shen Weici looked down and continued her embroidery: "When I gave Lady Zhang the sachet today, Lady Wen's expression already showed displeasure. There are some left over, so I will send them all out — in any case, I do not use them myself, and keeping them is of no use."

"When you go, just say this calming scent helps with sleep. The embroidery is my own work. The Laba Festival is coming soon, so it is simply a wish of good fortune."

Yuedeng acknowledged this and went.

She went first to the Second Branch. When she presented Lady Wen with her sachet, Lady Wen looked at it with disdain — but then when she saw the fine embroidery on it, her eyes went colder still. She passed it carelessly to the matron beside her and dismissed Yuedeng.

The moment Yuedeng left, the matron held the sachet and smelled it: "I've never smelled this before — not in any fragrance shop I've been to. It's really quite pleasant."

She brought it toward Lady Wen: "Madam, have a smell. Your sleep really has been poor lately — perhaps this is actually useful."

Lady Wen's expression remained cold. She took the sachet from the matron's hand, did not look at it again, and dropped it straight into the charcoal brazier: "What kind of second-rate thing is this? What good thing could come from that shabby little courtyard of hers?"

Matron Chang, reading Lady Wen's face, quietly kept her mouth shut.

In the Third Branch, Third Mistress Wang received the sachet and was quite delighted. She smelled the fragrance and admired the peony on the embroidery — so lifelike — and could not help praising it: "Third Young Miss has such skill with the needle. You would not know from looking at her that she never talks much, yet her hands are so gifted."

"I had no idea she could also blend fragrances. She really is a remarkable person."

She told a matron to give Yuedeng a few coins of reward, smiling: "It was kind of your young mistress to think of me — please give her my thanks."

Yuedeng hurried to refuse the reward that the matron brought forward, and bowed properly: "My young mistress says she was only hoping for something pleasing to look at. Coming to the Marquis Manor she has already relied on the kindness of every branch — she could not possibly accept a reward as well."

"My young mistress also said: this calming scent is called Five-Clear Fragrance, and it is a formula my young mistress blended herself. If Third Mistress finds it helpful for sleeping, please send word, and my young mistress will send more over."

Third Mistress Wang laughed: "Look how sharp and well-spoken this maid is. Go back and tell your young mistress I appreciate the thought — some day she must come and sit with me."

Yuedeng gave a soft sound of assent and retreated respectfully.

Third Mistress Wang watched Yuedeng's charming manner and could not help saying: "This Third Young Miss truly is a remarkable person — even her maids are trained so well."

"A young miss of such propriety — if she were in my courtyard, I certainly could not treat her badly either. With proper care and good guidance, she will marry well one day and will surely remember the kindness."

"What a pity for such a fine young woman."

The matron beside her joined in: "Indeed, Madam is so kind-hearted — the Second Branch really cannot compare with Madam."

Yuedeng went last to the Old Madam. Old Madam Shen accepted the sachet Yuedeng presented and remained cool as ever — but when she saw the Five Blessings and Longevity design on it, she spoke: "She has thought of me. It was kind of her to take the trouble."

She looked at Yuedeng and asked: "How has she been getting on with her health these past days?"

Yuedeng quickly replied: "Miss is much better. She often says she is grateful to the Old Madam for her concern, and for sending an imperial physician — the prescription has been very effective. After taking it for this time, she is healthier than before."

"Miss thinks of the Old Madam's kindness, and wanted to offer a small token of her appreciation."

chapters.title: She Does Not Dare Accept a Gift in Return
chapters.content:
The Old Madam heard Yuedeng's words and thought back to how she had requested the imperial physician for Shen Weici — that had only been to determine whether she was truly coughing blood. And yet Shen Weici had taken it as something to be grateful for.

She also thought about the last time Shen Weici coughed blood and was taken away by Song Zhang. Song Zhang would certainly not shield her — so it was possible the blood had been real after all.

The Old Madam nodded and told Yuedeng to go.

Yuedeng had not expected much tenderness or care from the Old Madam toward her young mistress in the first place, and now that she was dismissed, she left at a brisk and efficient pace.

Shen Weici was still doing embroidery, with Hexia and Yan'er helping to finish the edges.

Yuedeng sat across from Shen Weici, drank a sip of tea, and went through each household's reaction in turn. Shen Weici nodded and handed over what she had been working on: "Finish this one."

She reached for the next piece.

Shen Weici's needlework was exceptional — she could work the large part of a piece and leave the rest for the maids to follow, and they could still produce beautiful results from her pattern.

Yuedeng accepted it dutifully and, seeing Shen Weici pick up another, asked: "Why is Miss embroidering so many?"

Shen Weici said quietly: "I sent one person something, and so I sent everyone something — that way there is less for anyone to read into it."

"And there was also the matter of Zhang Tingyi, which damaged the Marquis Manor's reputation, and that affair started with me. Sending embroidered pieces around is a gesture of goodwill — making a good impression on people within the Manor is never a mistake."

She had not been working long when, close to midday, Laifu finally came — looking rather sheepish.

Shen Weici set down what she was doing, sat in the rattan chair, and told the maids in the room to step outside. Only then did she look at Laifu with a warm smile: "Come closer — no need to stand so stiffly."

Laifu did not dare look at Shen Weici's face. His eyes only fell on those alabaster fingertips and the soft drift of her skirt hem, and the very light fragrance that reached him. He nearly sank to his knees.

Faced with a Third Young Miss this gentle and lotus-pure, Laifu suddenly wished he could slap himself.

He shuffled forward a few steps, his eyes resting on the edge of an embroidered shoe he could see peeking out — the sparrow-and-branch design was very pretty.

Then a slender, pale hand extended toward him, cupping a few small silver beads. Her quiet, soft voice came: "Laifu, I have only been at the Manor a little over two months. There is much I do not know about this place and many people I am unfamiliar with. You helped me send letters, and I remember that. Please take this — consider it my way of thanking you."

Laifu looked at it in a daze. The fragrance from that hand was so warm. He had lived in this Manor his whole life — over twenty years — and no master had ever been this gentle with him.

He knew that Linchun Courtyard's monthly allowance was small, and had heard that just the other day the Old Madam had also docked several months of wages. He could not in good conscience accept this reward.

His eyes grew red. He dropped to his knees with a thud, bowed his head to the floor, and said: "This servant has wronged Third Young Miss. After Young Master Zhang left, every letter Third Young Miss sent — this servant did not deliver a single one."

Shen Weici looked down at Laifu kneeling on the floor, and bent to take him by the arm and help him stand. Her expression showed not the slightest anger. She only asked: "Why did you not send them?"

Laifu wiped his eyes, his face a picture of misery: "This servant dare not say. The person this servant could not afford to cross."

Shen Weici heard this and nodded. She did not press further, and only placed the silver beads in Laifu's palm: "Whether you sent them or not — I understand your difficulty. I will not blame you."

"You may go."

Laifu felt as though a gentle breeze had passed over his palm, scattering grace like a spring rain.

He stood looking at the silver beads in his hand, and felt a warmth behind his eyes. He dropped back to his knees: "This servant has wronged Third Young Miss. From now on, if Third Young Miss should ever need this servant's help, this servant will not hesitate for a moment."

Shen Weici smiled: "No need for that. But if I do need help, I will find you."

Only then did Laifu's heart settle a little. To be able to help someone as gentle, kind-hearted, and beautiful as this Third Young Miss — Laifu would be willing to do anything she asked.

After Laifu left, Shen Weici turned to look out the window. The light outside came through on a cold current of air and fell across her face. She narrowed her eyes.

The person who was too dangerous to cross was not difficult to guess.

That evening, Shen Weici sat on the bed and copied the Admonitions for Women. She was to submit the completed pages to the Old Madam in two days. She flipped through and estimated: ten pages per night would be exactly right.

Yuedeng, watching Shen Weici's fingers turn red from being exposed to the cold air, leaned over and said: "I can write too. Why not let me copy some for Miss?"

Shen Weici smiled: "Your handwriting — let us not go there."

Yuedeng propped her cheek in her hand and said: "Miss, did you notice how Young Master Zhang was looking at you today? I was standing behind you, and watching how his eyes stuck to Miss — it was really quite funny."

"He looked as though he is absolutely smitten."

"I bet he really does want to bring Miss home tomorrow."

Shen Weici pressed her lips together, and then felt, unexpectedly, a drift of sadness. She paused her brush.

Every gesture she had made before Zhang Yuanheng today — every motion had been something she had thought through inwardly first. She had never thought about feeling. The guilt that came now was something she had not planned for.

She was still lost in thought when Yuedeng suddenly called out: "Second Young Master."

Shen Weici startled. She turned — and Song Zhang was already walking in, utterly unconcerned that this was a young woman's private chamber, that it was a place even a true elder cousin should not enter casually.

Shen Weici had grown accustomed to Song Zhang's ways these past weeks. She did not argue and only asked quietly: "What brings Young Lord Song here at this hour? Is there something urgent?"

Song Zhang walked straight to Shen Weici's side, pressed one hand on the writing table and rested the other on the sword at his waist. He bent his head to scan the characters before her — precise and graceful, neat as printed type.

He also glanced at her fingers, still holding the brush, grown red with cold. Then he looked at Shen Weici's face.

Looking down at her like this always made him aware of a certain quality in her — the dark density of her hair, her eyes and brows lowered, the tiny mole at the corner of her eye faintly visible, making her already alluring peach-blossom eyes even more captivating.

And those lips — full and red as cherries — always drawing the mind involuntarily, always making him want to lower his head and take them.

He glanced with mild displeasure at Yuedeng standing in the corner — she was in the way. But this little maid was fiercely loyal, and telling her to leave would likely be refused.

He forced himself to use a voice that, for him, was about as close to pleasant as he got: "You still have time to copy the Admonitions for Women — is my pouch finished?"

Shen Weici had not expected Song Zhang to care so much about that pouch. He had now asked about it three times.

She paused and looked up at Song Zhang: "I will have it sent to Young Lord Song in two more days."

Song Zhang pulled a stool over and sat beside her. He gave a neutral sound, then said: "When you have finished the pouch, I will give you something in return if it pleases me."

Shen Weici, seeing Song Zhang settle in beside her as though intending to stay for some time, said quietly: "The pouch for Young Lord Song is what I ought to give. I would not dare accept a gift in return from Young Lord Song."

chapters.title: I Give What I Like
chapters.content:
Song Zhang noticed that Shen Weici always spoke to him in this courteous, soft-walled manner, and finding a fault in it was almost impossible.

He gave a cold snort: "I give what I like."

Shen Weici paused, but did not reply. She turned back and went on with the copying.

She had no wish to spend more time sparring with Song Zhang tonight. She still wanted to sleep early.

But before the tip of the brush had even touched the white paper, Song Zhang's large hand came down over it. Long, defined fingers — slightly tanned, nothing like Shen Yanli's fair cleanness, still bearing a few faint old scars, the calluses on his palms barely visible but hinting at great force.

He took a step toward her, and her gaze came only to his waist. She had barely turned her eyes away when Song Zhang's voice came from above, unhurried: "Only someone as obedient as you would sit here copying this."

He took the brush from Shen Weici's hand and let it fall onto the paper, where the scattering ink left a dark blot across the delicate characters: "Tomorrow I will bring you fifty pages of the Admonitions for Women. The handwriting will not be worse than yours."

"You just stay here and embroider my pouch in peace."

Shen Weici looked at the brush that had rolled onto the paper. She was quiet, then reached out, picked it up, and placed it back on the brush rest. She said softly: "I only have a few pages left."

"And I will certainly have the pouch sent to Young Lord Song."

Song Zhang raised an eyebrow. He saw Shen Weici reach for another sheet of paper, and the displeasure in him flared again. He bent down and brought his face close to hers, dark expression and all: "Not taking my kindness again?"

Shen Weici, seeing Song Zhang's face suddenly brought close, leaned back slightly and shook her head: "I am grateful for Young Lord Song's thought in helping me. But there are only a few pages remaining and it is truly not difficult."

"There is no need to write fifty new pages from scratch."

Song Zhang held Shen Weici's gaze, trying to read the truth behind her words.

She always declined him like this — without making any show of it, still and quiet. Gentle in nature, yet carrying a certain coolness.

He felt, for a moment, a sharp irritation with himself.

He thought: how was he any different from Zhang Yuanheng?

Perhaps he had also stepped into that half-hot-half-cold maze she created, and was already caught inside.

Something seemed to wake in him all at once. The cold sharpness in his eyes intensified. He narrowed them at her. The two of them were still in the candlelight. Song Zhang stood, pressed his lips down into a flat arc, and left with cold efficiency.

He had walked a short distance from the courtyard gate when Minhe came over, dragging a maid by the collar, and murmured: "Just now this maid was lurking near Linchun Courtyard, acting suspiciously. General, what shall be done with her?"

Song Zhang looked unhurriedly at the maid in Minhe's grip, then glanced at Minhe sideways: "Done with her for what? Just a Manor maid passing by."

He said his piece and walked on without another look at the maid.

Minhe stood for a moment, looking at the maid — who was white as a sheet with fright — then shook his head. When had the General become this magnanimous? That maid had obviously been watching Linchun Courtyard.

He hesitated, then released her and hurried after Song Zhang, murmuring at his side: "That maid saw the General going to Linchun Courtyard."

Song Zhang's expression was flat, his eyes unchanged: "Follow her. See which courtyard she belongs to. Do not disturb her."

Minhe acknowledged this and turned back.

In Linchun Courtyard, Yuedeng watched Song Zhang walk away and could not help whispering to Shen Weici: "Since the Second Young Master is willing to help Miss, why doesn't Miss let him?"

"I can see he has so much power — he could have it brought over first thing tomorrow morning. Why would Miss need to stay up late and write it herself?"

Shen Weici's gaze stayed on her brushwork, her eyes still, and said quietly: "He intercepted my letters."

Yuedeng did not follow at first, and said "Hm?"

Shen Weici said nothing more and continued writing in silence.

In those weeks, the only people who knew about her and Zhang Yuanheng — besides her father — was Song Zhang. Her father certainly would not have done it. The person too dangerous to cross could only be Song Zhang.

So she would not trust his goodwill.

Two days later, during Shen Weici's morning visit to Lady Wen's courtyard, she heard her father ask Lady Wen about the Earl's Manor visit. Lady Wen replied: "My lord, do not be anxious. The Earl's Manor will be coming to the Manor in a day or two to discuss the engagement."

Shen Rongshen nodded and looked at Shen Weici: "Prepare yourself well. Let us try to have your engagement settled before the new year."

Shen Weici nodded. But as she walked out of the Second Branch, her heart felt, strangely, not as light as she had expected.

In the past two days she had not sent another letter to Zhang Yuanheng — but Zhang Yuanheng had sent bird's nest, ginseng, and packages of medicinal herbs for cooking through her father.

She still remembered what her father had said when he had come, unusually, to her courtyard yesterday afternoon and passed over the things Zhang Yuanheng had sent.

Her father had said: if she needed anything, she could ask her stepmother — the Marquis Manor had everything. Having the Earl's Manor bring things over would create talk again if it got out, and she should also be mindful not to give people more to say.

Shen Weici had understood her father's meaning immediately. The Manor could choose not to give — but they could not let the outside world know they had not given, as that would reflect on them. She had listened and agreed.

But the warmth she had felt was gradually cooling.

She had coughed blood twice — though not genuinely — and her father had not once shown any real concern, had never sent anything to her courtyard, had never changed the food she received. Even the decoctions and medicines had been managed entirely by her own small courtyard's maids.

Shen Weici had not truly wanted those tonics and supplements. She had also never dared ask for them.

Back in Linchun Courtyard, she took the completed pages of the Admonitions for Women to the Old Madam.

Old Madam Shen leaned in her armchair and watched a matron receive the stack of papers from Shen Weici. The pages were thick — but organized with remarkable neatness. More remarkably, the characters on every sheet were uniformly beautiful and precise. She pulled one out at random: the same handwriting, the same exacting standard.

The Old Madam was faintly surprised. No matter which page she drew, it was as if it had come from the same print block. The care that had gone into it was unmistakable.

She looked up at Shen Weici standing before her — correct and graceful in a pale yellow half-high-collar jacket, jade hairpin in her hair, jadeite earrings at her ears, brows soft and downcast, both hands folded in front of her, bearing and manner impossible to fault.

She remembered telling her to dress herself up properly — to wear a few more pieces of jewelry.

For a moment the Old Madam felt a stab of something she could not quite name. Here was a young woman who had grown up in the countryside without any formal family education — and she kept giving the Old Madam cause to look at her differently.

The handwriting was better than Zhaozhao's. Fifty pages, complete, not a single character skimped on. The steadiness of spirit that required — how many young women would actually have it? Even the most well-bred girls tended to cut corners somewhere.

She handed the pages to the matron beside her and looked at Shen Weici: "The sachet you sent — the fragrance inside was blended by you yourself?"

Shen Weici answered honestly: "In the old days, my mother did not sleep well at night, so I read through books and went into the hills to gather herbs and flowers. She was able to rest more peacefully after that."

The Old Madam nodded. She looked at the figure standing against the light — white-skinned and gentle — and said: "A filial child."

chapters.title: There Is No Logic to Be Found Here
chapters.content:
Because of the wind the coughing-blood affair had stirred, the Old Madam's impression of Shen Weici had not been good.

She had lain awake thinking about the rumors for several nights in a row. But two days before, a matron had hung the sachet Shen Weici sent at her bedside, and she had truly slept soundly for the whole night — and then again the next.

Now seeing Shen Weici accept her punishment so properly, and noticing the unhurried composure she carried about her, the Old Madam found her impression of Shen Weici quietly shifting.

A matron had said to her: Shen Weici did not have that kind of influence — she was a girl with no connections who had come from the countryside to seek shelter. She could not possibly have spread a rumor that traveled so far and so fast.

The Old Madam had thought about it afterward and decided there was sense in that. The rumors outside had still not died down, and her own reputation had been damaged — but the particular fury she had felt toward Shen Weici had diminished.

After all, if she were truly to hold Shen Weici responsible for something in this affair, it would only be that she had coughed blood at such a convenient moment — but an imperial physician had come and taken her pulse, and it could not be faked.

The Old Madam thought it through once more, then asked, as an aside: "How has the health been getting along?"

Shen Weici replied: "I have caused the Old Madam worry. These past days I have been much better."

The Old Madam had nothing particular to say to Shen Weici. Unlike Shen Zhaozhao, she had not much feeling for this granddaughter — even if the girl had made a slightly better impression on her today, she felt no real tenderness toward her.

She asked a few more questions, then told Shen Weici to go back and rest.

The Old Madam's close matron watched Shen Weici's unhurried retreating figure, and could not help bending toward the Old Madam's ear: "This old servant has noticed that the Third Young Miss is not at all wanting compared to young women from established families — if anything, she stands out somewhat."

"She is also of marriageable age. If a proper match is found for her, she could be settled into a fine household. That would benefit the Marquis Manor, restore the Old Madam's reputation for being kind-hearted, and the talk outside would have nothing left to stand on."

The Old Madam heard this and the hand holding her teacup paused. She murmured: "What you say is not without reason."

"I heard her stepmother went to the Yiyong Earl's Manor two days ago about her engagement."

She paused again: "Go and call Lady Wen here. I have a few words to say to her."

The matron withdrew to send for Lady Wen.

After Shen Weici returned, she called for the maids to do needlework. By the afternoon, she looked at the pouches laid out on the table — she had been working on them whenever she had a free moment in recent days, and they were now finished at last.

Yuedeng was concerned about her hands: "Miss has poked herself in several places. The fingers will need at least a month to heal."

Shen Weici smiled: "I will not be doing any more embroidery for a while."

That evening she told Yuedeng to take the pouch to Guansong Residence. If Song Zhang was not there, she should leave it with a maid.

But a short while later Yuedeng came back, panting, with the pouch still in hand, and said: "I had just gotten there when the Second Young Master was coming back. And he just looked at me once and said Miss sending something without coming in person showed no sincerity — Miss must come personally, otherwise he would not accept it."

She stamped her foot: "How difficult this person is to deal with. He would not even let me through the courtyard gate."

Shen Weici took the pouch from Yuedeng's hand, said a few words to soothe her, and told her to bring a cloak.

Shen Weici knew Song Zhang's character well enough — trying to reason with him was pointless. She only wanted to give it to him as quickly as possible and have no further dealings between them.

She put on the cloak, fastened the tie, and Yuedeng pressed a hand warmer into Shen Weici's hands: "Take this, Miss. It is cold on the path."

"I even made a little cloth sleeve for it — wrap it up and tuck it in. It will keep Miss warm."

Shen Weici looked down to accept it, and the warmth entered her palms at once, gradually thawing her cold fingertips.

Rather than taking the path that went past the Second Branch, Shen Weici went around the lake, cutting through the back garden by the false mountain, along a small path that connected to many parts of the rear garden — no one could be certain where it led.

The path did pass a long covered corridor and a stone bridge, which was not so easy to walk at night.

Yuedeng asked: "Miss, why are we going this way?"

Shen Weici kept her eyes on the ground: "It is always better to be careful. I was taken away by Young Lord Song last time and have since been going back and forth to his quarters. If that is noticed, it will not look good."

"If anyone thinks Young Lord Song is helping me on purpose, that would be worse still."

Yuedeng made a sound of understanding and held Shen Weici's arm as they walked.

But as she walked along, Shen Weici suddenly felt herself pulled sideways with force. Before she could make a sound, someone's hand covered her mouth. Her young mistress's low voice sounded in her ear: "Not a sound."

Yuedeng's hand found rough stone, and she realized she had been pulled behind a false mountain.

She did not dare make a sound. Then she saw, not far away, light approaching — a furtive silhouette moving along the very path they had just walked, circling several times as though searching for someone, then murmuring in puzzlement: "Where did they go?"

The voice was a maid's, faintly unfamiliar. Yuedeng now understood: someone had been following them.

She pressed tight against the corner of the false mountain, not daring to breathe.

After a while, the figure failed to find anyone and moved off in another direction.

Shen Weici watched that direction — directly toward Song Zhang's Guansong Residence. She understood that someone had already begun to take note of the connection between her and Song Zhang.

Yuedeng whispered in the darkness: "Miss, shall we come out now?"

Shen Weici said quietly: "Wait a little longer."

Coming out now would likely bring them face to face with the maid who had just been looking for them. She would know they had been heading toward Song Zhang's quarters.

This section of path was not far. Once the maid found no one, she would naturally turn back.

After a while, the maid did retrace her steps, passing close to where they were. Once she had gone, Shen Weici leaned close to Yuedeng's ear: "Follow behind her. Just follow her lantern light — see which courtyard she belongs to. Be careful. Keep your distance."

Yuedeng looked toward Shen Weici worriedly in the darkness: "But Miss will be alone with no lantern — how will Miss walk?"

Shen Weici replied: "Do not worry about me. It is not far from here. I can feel my way. Go quickly before you lose sight of her. Meet me back at Linchun Courtyard."

Yuedeng, knowing she could not delay, quickly slipped out of the false mountain and, keeping low, followed the light ahead.

Shen Weici came out behind Yuedeng. She held the extinguished lantern in her hand. Fortunately the moon was bright tonight and she could just make out the path. She lifted her skirt hem and made her way toward Guansong Residence.

The path was a small one, though, with dense undergrowth on either side that was hard to see clearly. Something caught her foot, and she stumbled. Something sharp — the corner of a stone — raked across her ankle. The pain made cold sweat break across her brow.

She breathed in slowly, stood, and moved the ankle. The bone seemed uninjured — only a little painful. She rose and continued walking.

The lanterns at the gate of Guansong Residence were bright enough to be seen from some distance. Shen Weici walked toward that light, and the path became easier.

The guards at the gate saw her and without asking a single question stepped aside to let her through.

A maid waiting at the door said quietly to Shen Weici: "The Second Young Master is in the inner study. Third Young Miss may go straight in."

Shen Weici noticed that the maid stayed outside at the gate without following her in, and pressed her lips together, gathered her sleeves, and stepped over the threshold.

She had been to Song Zhang's study twice before and knew the way well enough. But the room had not a single maid in it, which mildly surprised her.

Coming to a curtain, she drew a quiet breath and pushed it aside. One glance and she saw Song Zhang seated behind a rosewood desk.

His face was half in lamplight — the sharp-sculpted lines of it proud and cold. His eyes, always arrogant, looked across at her and revealed nothing of his feelings.

Shen Weici lowered her gaze and walked to him in a few steps.

chapters.title: Feeling
chapters.content:
The light in the room was not as bright as it had been on other visits. Only two gilded gauze lamps were burning. The window was shut tight, and a floor brazier in the corner kept the room quite warm.

Shen Weici had come in from the cold outside, and as the warmth touched her, a faint blush began to rise in her cheeks.

Her cloak was still around her shoulders, its hood let down. She had no intention of staying long, and had not moved to take the cloak off.

Her pale fingers came out from beneath the cloak and held out the pouch: "This is the one embroidered for Young Lord Song. If Young Lord Song does not find it too humble, please accept it."

From the moment Shen Weici had walked in, Song Zhang's gaze had not left her.

The pale yellow jacket suited her complexion particularly well today. In the lamplight, her skin seemed to glow with its own luminescence.

At her earlobes swayed two small jadeite earrings, striking against that smooth face, the glancing light from them casting trailing ripples across her cheek. The effect was arrestingly lovely.

She had only added one pair of earrings, and already Song Zhang found he could not look away — the tie at her collar, the back of the wide sleeve with its sky-blue spiral-square pattern, all of it carrying a quality of languid, weary elegance.

To say nothing of those peach-blossom eyes under those brushstroke brows, those cherry lips — enough to carry a man's soul off entirely.

Song Zhang's gaze roamed over Shen Weici for a long while before finally settling on those pale fingers, half-hidden behind the wide sleeve. The pouch was small, but exquisitely beautiful at a glance.

He lowered his eyes, reached out and took it. The blue-ground silk was embroidered with a golden lion playing with a pearl — both fierce and dignified, and the lion also being a symbol of warding off evil. She had given this thought.

Something warmed in Song Zhang's expression. His thumb moved over the fine embroidery. A pouch of this kind was something a man would wear on his person — and the thought gave him a small, pleasurable stir.

He glanced at her, with her brows and eyes still downcast: "Did you do all of this yourself? No help from the maids?"

Shen Weici did not look up at Song Zhang. She shook her head: "No."

Song Zhang was more pleased still.

The pouch still carried the faint, pleasant fragrance that clung to her. To think of it lying in her hands day after day, sewn with patient care — his body went taut, and a warmth stirred in him.

He held the pouch in his hand. The corner of his lip curved upward without his meaning it to: "You put in the effort, so I will give you something in return."

Shen Weici had only a moment's awareness of a shadow falling over her — and when she came back to herself, Song Zhang was already on his feet, bent over her. He took her wrist in his hand, and slipped a bracelet from his own wrist down onto hers.

Then his low voice came: "Women like wearing these things, do they not? I thought this color would suit you best. I chose it myself, and you are the only one who gets this treatment."

Shen Weici looked at the bracelet now on her wrist. The color was very translucent — a pale blush smoke-white, like flower and mist together.

Women did like wearing such things. But Shen Weici had stopped wearing jewelry of any kind after she was ten.

Even in Yuyang, the women there who could not afford jade would have a pair of silver bracelets made from a template. But she had always been saving every copper coin she had, and had never once allowed herself such things.

Now, with this beautiful bracelet on her wrist, she found herself slightly unaccustomed to it.

Song Zhang noticed Shen Weici's slight daze, and looked down again at the fingers he still held — small and white, as if they could glow in the dark. Tanned and pale side by side — a striking sight.

Shen Weici drew her hand free from Song Zhang's hold and tucked it back inside the cloak. She looked up at Song Zhang, then lowered her eyes and said with precise care: "Weici thanks Young Lord Song for the kind thought."

"As it is already night, I will go first."

She curtseyed toward Song Zhang and turned to walk toward the door.

Song Zhang suddenly caught her by the wrist. Frowning, he looked down at Shen Weici's shoe, just peeking out from below the hem.

When he had put the bracelet on her wrist earlier, he had already noticed something slightly off.

Shen Weici became aware of Song Zhang's gaze. Having a man look at her shoe like this felt uncomfortable, and she tried to draw her foot back under her skirt hem. But Song Zhang suddenly swept her up and set her on the chair, crouched down, and lifted her skirt hem. He took hold of her embroidered shoe.

It was small even in his hand. But on the snow-white fabric there was a smear of blood — quite noticeable against the pale color.

Song Zhang's dark eyes came up to look at her: "When did this happen?"

Being held this way — a man not closely acquainted with her holding her shoe — her face had gone pale, and there was a kind of helpless uncertainty in her usually composed eyes. She pulled her leg back, but could not match his grip.

She did not answer him. She only said, a little urgently: "Young Lord Song, please let me go first."

"It is only a scrape. It is not serious."

Song Zhang saw that Shen Weici would not answer. His brow was heavy. Without waiting for her to react, he removed her embroidered shoe with no ceremony, revealing the white stocking inside, also bearing a smear of blood.

There was not much blood — only a stain spreading into a small patch — but it looked startling.

Song Zhang glanced at Shen Weici, and in the face of her alarmed eyes, with calm efficiency pulled off her white stocking, revealing her white-porcelain foot beneath.

At the ankle there was a small cut — not wide, but a little deep, as though caught on the sharp corner of a stone.

He stood and went to get the medicine, then turned back to her with a threat: "Do not move."

"Or I will tie you down."

Shen Weici froze. Her fingers pressed into the edge of the chair, tightening very slightly.
